ex.zh: “我太不明智了，竟让你到我自己都知之不深的人家去；他们心肠也许是好的，可满脑子俗气，没有教养，对年轻人尽是这些粗俗的念头。

senses.d: impoliteness resulting from ignorance

ex.zh: 达西先生似乎为姨母的没教养有点难为情，没有作声。

ex.zh: 他立刻觉得她有了某种说不清的变化。

senses.d: not well dressed

ex.zh: “昨晚我在巷子里看见一个衣衫褴褛的流浪汉，”霍尔德先生说。

senses.d: poorly supplied with physical equipment

ex.zh: “后来我常想，我对这样一场经历准备得多么不足。

ex.zh: 我走进停放我那不幸而可敬的朋友遗体的舱房。

ex.t: John clapped his hands on the ill-fated pirate’s mouth to stifle the dying groan.
ex.zh: 约翰用手捂住这倒霉海盗的嘴，压住他临死的呻吟。

senses.d: usually used of a face

ex.zh: 而实际上，据他判断，第一空降场的大多数人都矮小、黝黑、不好看。

senses.d: not the right size or shape

ex.zh: 路人惊奇地瞥着这阴沉粗壮的少年，他穿着粗劣不合身的衣裳，却陪着这样一位优雅秀气的姑娘。

senses.d: not given careful consideration

ex.zh: 她到这里来，是世上最不幸、最失算的事！

ex.t: Allow me to say, Lady Catherine, that the arguments with which you have supported this extraordinary application have been as frivolous as the application was ill-judged.
ex.zh: 夫人，请容我说一句：您用来支持这番离奇要求的理由，跟这要求本身一样站不住脚。

senses.d: having an irritable and unpleasant disposition

ex.t: His marriage was now fast approaching; and she was at length so far resigned as to think it inevitable, and even repeatedly to say, in an ill-natured tone, that she “wished they might be happy.”
ex.zh: 他的婚期如今快到了；她终于也认了命，觉得这是免不了的，甚至一再恶声恶气地说她“但愿他们幸福”。

ex.t: He has not an ill-natured look.
ex.zh: 他脸上并没有凶相。

ex.t: I have thought sometimes that it was the disposition of her child which weighed upon her mind, for I have never met so utterly spoiled and so ill-natured a little creature.
ex.zh: 我有时想，是她孩子的性情压在她心头，因为我从没见过这样被彻底惯坏、脾气这样坏的小东西。

senses.d: marked by or promising bad fortune- W.H.Prescott
x: their business venture was doomed from the start
an ill-fated business venture

ex.t: There was no law, not even an unwritten law, against frequenting the Chestnut Tree Cafe, yet the place was somehow ill-omened.
ex.zh: 没有法律，甚至没有不成文的法律，禁止去栗树咖啡馆，可那地方总有点不祥。

ex.t: It was an ill-omened place.
ex.zh: 这是个不吉利的地方。

senses.d: having an unpleasant smell

ex.t: The night was hot, and the shop, close shut and surrounded by so foul a neighbourhood, was ill-smelling.
ex.zh: 夜里很热，店面关得严实，四周又是那么肮脏的街坊，气味很难闻。

senses.d: annoyed and irritable

ex.t: Just then a horse's head looked over from the stall beyond; the ears were laid back, and the eye looked rather ill-tempered.
ex.zh: 正在这时，再过去一个马位上探出一个马头，耳朵向后贴着，眼神挺不客气。

ex.t: “I should take him, even on my slight acquaintance, to be an ill-tempered man.”
ex.zh: “就说我这浅浅的一点相识，我也会当他是个脾气坏的人。”

ex.zh: “我怕，汉内，你这次来得不是时候。”

ex.t: I beg you will not put it into Lizzy's head to be vexed by his ill-treatment, for he is such a disagreeable man that it would be quite a misfortune to be liked by him.
“I beg you will not put it into Lizzy’s head to be vexed by his ill-treatment, for he is such a disagreeable man that it would be quite a misfortune to be liked by him.
ex.zh: “我求你，别在丽琪心里种下为他那无礼而气恼的念头；因为他是那么讨人厌的男子，被他喜欢上倒是一场不幸。

ex.t: “In the first place, I may say that I have met, on the whole, with no actual ill-treatment from Mr. and Mrs. Rucastle.
ex.zh: “首先，我可以说，总的来说，鲁卡斯尔先生和太太并没有真正虐待我。

senses.d: cruel or inhumane treatment
x: the child showed signs of physical abuse

ex.t: We are not on friendly terms, and it always gives me pain to meet him, but I have no reason for avoiding him but what I might proclaim to all the world--a sense of very great ill-usage, and most painful regrets at his being what he is.
ex.zh: 我们彼此并不友好，见着他总叫我难过；可我要避开他，理由只有一条，且是能向全世界宣布的——我觉得自己受了极大的亏待，又为他竟是那样一个人而痛心悔恨。

ex.t: He spoke in a slow staccato fashion, choosing his words with care, and gave the impression generally of a man of learning and letters who had had ill-usage at the hands of fortune.
ex.zh: 他说话慢而断续，字斟句酌，给人总的印象是个有学问、有文墨的人，只是受了命运的亏待。

senses.d: treat badly
x: This boss abuses his workers
She is always stepping on others to get ahead

ex.t: I don't ill-use my horse for the sake of it; none of you can say I do.
ex.zh: 我不是为了乐意才虐待我的马；你们谁也不能说我乐意。

senses.d: (of persons) taken advantage of
x: after going out of his way to help his friend get the job he felt not appreciated but used

ex.t: If I was to stop half-a-crown for it, you'd think yourself ill-used, I'll be bound?"
ex.zh: 要是我为这个扣你半个克朗，你准觉得自己受了委屈，我敢打赌？”

ex.t: "And yet," said Scrooge, "you don't think me ill-used, when I pay a day's wages for no work."
ex.zh: “可是，”斯克鲁奇说，“我白付一天工钱，你倒不觉得我受了委屈。”

ex.t: Of course, it is a very bad habit; but I am sure, if all she says be true, she must have been very ill-used before she came here.
ex.zh: 当然，这是个很坏的毛病；可我敢说，要是她说的都是真的，那她来这儿以前准是被人糟践得厉害。

senses.d: treat badly
x: This boss abuses his workers
She is always stepping on others to get ahead

ex.t: They were just going home to dinner when the footman came down to the stable to say that Joe was wanted directly in master's private room; there was a man brought up for ill-using horses, and Joe's evidence was wanted.
ex.zh: 他们正要回家吃饭，跟班的下来到马厩说，老爷叫乔马上到他的书房去；有人因为虐待马被带来了，要乔去作证。

senses.d: prohibited by law or by official or accepted rules
x: an illegal chess move

ex.t: This was not illegal (nothing was illegal, since there were no longer any laws), but if detected it was reasonably certain that it would be punished by death, or at least by twenty-five years in a forced-labour camp.
ex.zh: 这不算违法（没有什么是违法的，因为早已没有法律了），可一旦被发现，几乎可以肯定要处死，至少也是二十五年劳改营。

ex.t: I have done nothing actionable from the first, but as long as you keep that door locked you lay yourself open to an action for assault and illegal constraint.”
ex.zh: 我从头到尾没做过一件能让人起诉的事；可你只要把门锁着，就犯了殴打和非法拘禁的罪，随时可以被起诉。”

senses.d: in an illegal manner

ex.t: “If I am Mr. Neville St. Clair, then it is obvious that no crime has been committed, and that, therefore, I am illegally detained.”
ex.zh: “如果我真是内维尔·圣克莱尔先生，那显而易见，并没有犯下什么罪，因此我是被非法拘留的。”

senses.d: in a manner disapproved or not allowed by custom

ex.zh: 事实上，要为新话的不正统用途服务，只能靠把其中一些词不合法地译回旧话。

ex.zh: 那里有行贿、徇私、各种敲诈，有同性恋和卖淫，甚至有私酿的土豆酒。

an inability to read

ex.zh: 要是机器被有意用于这个目的，饥饿、过劳、肮脏、文盲和疾病在几代人之内就能消除。

ex.zh: 温斯顿找到两张皱巴巴、脏兮兮的钞票递过去，帕森斯记在一个小本子上，笔迹工整，像一个不识字的人写出的工整字。

senses.d: impairment of normal physiological function affecting part or all of an organism

There was a time in the youth of the world when Goods and Ills entered equally into the concerns of men, so that the Goods did not prevail to make them altogether blessed, nor the Ills to make them wholly miserable.

But owing to the foolishness of mankind the Ills multiplied greatly in number and increased in strength, until it seemed as though they would deprive the Goods of all share in human affairs, and banish them from the earth.

ex.zh: 太阳还高在天上；在它落下去藏到你那些雪峰后面、去照亮另一个世界之前，你就会听完我的故事，可以决断了。

ex.t: The windows of the room had before been darkened, and I felt a kind of panic on seeing the pale yellow light of the moon illuminate the chamber.
ex.zh: 屋子的窗先前是暗着的；我一见月亮那淡黄的光照进房里，就感到一种惊惶。

ex.t: No, but put a sky-light on top of his head to illuminate inwards.
ex.zh: 不，在他头顶上开一扇天窗，朝里照。

Under the over-swinging lamps--swinging ever brighter in the better streets, and ever dimmer in the worse--and by lighted shops, gay crowds, illuminated coffee-houses, and theatre-doors, to one of the city gates.
ex.zh: 在那来回摇晃的灯下——在好一些的街上越摇越亮，在差一些的街上越摇越暗——经过亮着灯的店铺、欢闹的人群、灯火通明的咖啡馆和戏院门口，来到一座城门。

ex.t: The illuminated village had seized hold of the tocsin, and, abolishing the lawful ringer, rang for joy.
ex.zh: 灯火通明的村子把警钟抢到了手，废掉了合法的敲钟人，欢天喜地地敲起来。

ex.zh: 那骑马人又哒哒地冲下山，穿过街道，这时村子正在亮起来。

ex.t: But, spite of all this, I could see no compass before me to steer by; though it seemed but a minute since I had been watching the card, by the steady binnacle lamp illuminating it.
ex.zh: 可尽管如此，我面前却看不见可以照着操舵的罗盘；虽然我看那刻度盘，似乎还不过一分钟——那时罗经柜的灯稳稳地照着它。

ex.zh: “艾米那幅彩饰在哪儿摆着么？

ex.zh: 他把自己的铺位弄成一盏阿拉丁的神灯，然后躺进去；所以哪怕在最漆黑的夜里，这船的黑壳子里仍旧装着一团光明。

senses.d: an erroneous mental representation

x: they have the illusion that I am very wealthy

“Well—the general air, the style, the self-possession, the—the—illusion—you know”, laughed Laurie, breaking down and helping himself out of his quandary with the new word.
ex.zh: “呃——那种气派，那种派头，那份镇定，那——那——幻影纱——你懂。”劳里笑着，话接不下去，只好拿这个新词把自己从窘里救出来。

ex.t: But there were also times when they had the illusion not only of safety but of permanence.
ex.zh: 可也有些时候，他们不但觉得自己安全，还觉得这能长久。

ex.zh: 她像从一尊倒下的偶像前转过身去，又发现了别的事，很快就把她的浪漫幻想驱散了。

ex.t: She was usually in love with somebody, and, as her passion was never returned, she had kept all her illusions.
ex.zh: 她通常总在爱着某个人，而因为她的热情从无回应，她保住了全部幻想。

ex.zh: 那壁炉是旧式的，许久以前由某个荷兰商人砌成，四周围铺着古怪的荷兰瓷砖，上面画的是《圣经》故事。

ex.t: Some, however, have already gained publicity through the papers, and others have not offered a field for those peculiar qualities which my friend possessed in so high a degree, and which it is the object of these papers to illustrate.
ex.zh: 不过，其中有些已经通过报纸公之于众；另一些则没有提供余地，来展示我朋友那种高超卓绝的独特才能——而这些文字的目的正是要说明这种才能。

supply with illustrations

ex.zh: 到起居室去，安妮——先把脚弄干净，别放苍蝇进去——把壁炉架上那张画片给我拿来。

ex.t: “These bits of lace are fastened under the chin with a rosebud, so,” and Meg illustrated by putting on the bonnet and regarding him with an air of calm satisfaction that was irresistible.
ex.zh: “这些花边用一朵玫瑰花苞系在下巴底下，这么着。”梅格说着戴上帽子示范，带着一种镇静的满意神气看他，那神气叫人抵挡不住。

ex.t: So the lad was looking rather sulky, as with listless fingers he turned over the pages of an elaborately illustrated edition of Manon Lescaut that he had found in one of the book-cases.
ex.zh: 于是这年轻人脸色有些阴沉，懒懒地翻着一本装帧精美的插图本《曼侬·莱斯科》，那是他从某个书柜里翻出来的。

senses.d: clarify by giving an example of

ex.zh: 单这一桩，就足以说明我要讲的那个显而易见的事实。

ex.zh: 姐姐们叫她“小拉斐尔”，她画画确有天赋；临花、设计仙女，或者用些古怪的画儿给故事配图的时候，她最快活不过。

ex.t: It was a museum used for propaganda displays of various kinds--scale models of rocket bombs and Floating Fortresses, waxwork tableaux illustrating enemy atrocities, and the like.
ex.zh: 那是个博物馆，用来做各种宣传展览——火箭弹和浮动堡垒的比例模型，表现敌人暴行的蜡像场景，诸如此类。

ex.zh: 咱们就说，为了打个比方、说明一下，他在病重的时候惯常在一座小铁炉上干活。

ex.zh: 他抬眼去看洛里先生的脸时，那样子就像他打的比方。

ex.zh: 乔瞟了一眼那张纸，看见一幅“好看”的插图，由疯子、尸体、恶棍和一条毒蛇拼成。

ex.zh: 她教我怎么把披肩裹在肩上；我离开那小屋时，活脱是彭斯诗里插图那种苏格兰人。

ex.t: “Is it the immediate object of this confidence, that you may at once ascertain that, with my knowledge?”
ex.zh: “你这次吐露心事，当前的目的是不是想在我知情的情况下，马上把这一点弄明白？”

senses.d: without delay or hesitation; with no time intervening
x: he answered immediately
found an answer straightaway

senses.d: near or close by

senses.d: bearing an immediate relation
x: this immediately concerns your future

and his answering immediately to the last question, 'Oh, the eldest Miss Bennet, beyond a doubt: there cannot be two opinions on that point.'"
The fish that you have tattooed immediately above your right wrist could only have been done in China.

senses.d: long past; beyond the limits of memory or tradition or recorded history
x: time immemorial

Now, I still think that for this box of matches to have escaped the wear of time for immemorial years was a most strange, as for me it was a most fortunate, thing.
Nevertheless, the old sea-traditions, the immemorial credulities, popularly invested this old Manxman with preternatural powers of discernment.
ex.zh: 然而，那些古老的海上传说、那些太古以来的轻信，在大众心里赋予了这位马恩岛老人一种超自然的眼力。

senses.d: unusually great in size or amount or degree or especially extent or scope- W.R.Inge

huge country estates

I pass my whole life, miss, in turning an immense pecuniary Mangle."

senses.d: to an exceedingly great extent or degree

ex.zh: 伯特伦送她一枚钻石戒指、一串红宝石项链，还告诉她他们要去欧洲度蜜月，因为他富得不得了。

ex.t: But he admired Anne immensely, and was puffed up with pride over the prospect of driving to White Sands with that slim, upright figure beside him.
ex.zh: 可他极佩服安妮，一想到要赶着车去白沙，身边坐着那挺直苗条的身影，就得意得鼓起来。

senses.d: unusual largeness in size or extent or number

ex.t: Already we are boldly launched upon the deep; but soon we shall be lost in its unshored, harbourless immensities.
ex.zh: 我们已大胆地驶入深海；可不久我们就要在那无岸、无港的浩瀚里迷失。

ex.t: Is it that by its indefiniteness it shadows forth the heartless voids and immensities of the universe, and thus stabs us from behind with the thought of annihilation, when beholding the white depths of the milky way?
ex.zh: 是不是因为它的不确定，它才隐约映出宇宙那无心的虚空与无限，于是在我们望着银河那白色的深处时，从背后用消灭的念头刺我们一下？

senses.d: unusual largeness in size or extent or number

ex.t: The intense concentration of self in the middle of such a heartless immensity, my God! who can tell it?
ex.zh: 自我在这样无情的浩瀚当中那样极度地凝聚起来，我的上帝！谁说得出来？

senses.d: thrust or throw into

senses.d: devote (oneself) fully to

senses.d: enclose or envelop completely, as if by swallowing

senses.d: cause to be immersed

ex.zh: 我处在这种情况下，做着最可憎的活，陷在一种孤独里，没有任何东西能有一刻把我的心从眼前的场景拉开，我的精神便变得不平衡；我变得烦躁而神经紧张。

senses.d: close in time; about to occur

some people believe the day of judgment is close at hand

We are still surrounded by mountains of ice, still in imminent danger of being crushed in their conflict.
ex.zh: 我们仍被冰山围着，仍随时有在冰的冲撞里被压碎的危险。

ex.t: We were in the most imminent peril, but as we could only remain passive, my chief attention was occupied by my unfortunate guest whose illness increased in such a degree that he was entirely confined to his bed.
ex.zh: 我们处在最急的危险里；可我们只能干等着，我的主要心思就放在我那不幸的客人身上——他的病加重到完全起不了床。

ex.zh: 她能一连几个钟头几乎不动地坐在床上，抱着他的小妹妹，一个两三岁的孩子，瘦小、多病、一声不响，脸瘦得像猴子。

ex.t: O'Brien motioned with his head to the man in the white coat, who had stood immobile throughout the proceedings.
ex.zh: 奥布莱恩朝穿白大褂的人点了点头；那人整个过程一直一动不动站着。

ex.t: He hesitated for some moments, with a strangely immobile smile upon his face.
ex.zh: 他犹豫了一会儿，脸上带着一种古怪的、静止不动的笑。

ex.zh: 没有谁比我更爱你的弟弟了”——他说时眼里来了泪——“可我们不该做出过度的悲伤的样子，来加重他们的不幸，这不也是对活着的人的一份本分吗？

senses.d: to a degree that exceeds the bounds or reason or moderation

ex.zh: 可我问她时，她笑得没了分寸，把我的问题大声重复了一遍，然后告诉我她跟一个女朋友住在一家旅馆里。

senses.d: offer as a sacrifice by killing or by giving up to destruction

immolate the valuables at the temple

ex.t: That, he had been the prisoner’s friend, but, at once in an auspicious and an evil hour detecting his infamy, had resolved to immolate the traitor he could no longer cherish in his bosom, on the sacred altar of his country.
ex.zh: 他本来是犯人的朋友，可是在一个既吉利又凶险的时刻察觉了他的邪恶，便决心把这个他再也不能放在怀里珍爱的叛徒，献祭在祖国的圣坛上。

senses.d: deliberately violating accepted principles of right and wrong

a base, degrading way of life

ex.zh: 书无所谓道德或不道德。

ex.zh: “一切影响都是不道德的——从科学观点看是不道德的。”

ex.zh: “一切闲话的根据，是一桩不道德的确定。”亨利勋爵点起一支烟说。

senses.d: the quality of not being in accord with standards of right or good conduct

ex.zh: 例如，他的性生活完全由两个新话词规范：SEXCRIME（性方面的不道德）和 GOODSEX（贞洁）。

ex.t: I consider that for any man of culture to accept the standard of his age is a form of the grossest immorality.”
ex.zh: 我认为，任何有教养的人接受自己时代的标准，都是最粗鄙的不道德。”

senses.d: a person (such as an author) of enduring fame

senses.d: any supernatural being worshipped as controlling some part of the world or some aspect of life or who is the personification of a force

Long John Silver, he is called, and has lost a leg; but that I regarded as a recommendation, since he lost it in his country's service, under the immortal Hawke.

ex.t: God was not a blind force, and immortality was not a pretty fable, but a blessed fact.
ex.zh: 上帝不是一股盲目的力量，永生也不是个好听的寓言，而是一件有福的事实。

ex.zh: 等他四下找一个不那么难缠的姑娘来写进曲子里、使她不朽时，记忆却极顺从地送来了一个。

senses.d: a person (such as an author) of enduring fame
x: Shakespeare is one of the immortals

senses.d: any supernatural being worshipped as controlling some part of the world or some aspect of life or who is the personification of a force
not subject to death

ex.zh: 他告诉我的那些听着已经够大，可真正的事大得没边，以至于他这个查明真相的人，想把它整个占为己有。

ex.zh: 那幽灵照旧一动不动。

ex.zh: 那额头上的表情——先前那样格外引起他注意、如今一动不动的——已经加深成了痛苦与恐怖。

ex.zh: 那些不可移动的铭文里，含着怎样的绝望！

ex.zh: 她是海上的吃人者，几乎用不着那只警觉的眼，因为她浮在自己名字的恐怖里，没人敢惹。

ex.zh: 我知道宫廷的势力是怎么回事，也知道贵族的豁免是怎么回事，我料想这事永远不会有人过问；可我想让自己心里松一松。

ex.zh: 命运太强大了，它那些不可更改的法则早已判定了我的彻底而可怕的毁灭。

ex.zh: 然而，尽管这样一成不变，可敬的比勒达船长身上还是有点欠缺常理的一贯。

ex.zh: 这整出戏早已不可更改地定下了。在这大洋滚动之前十亿年，你我就已经排演过了。

ex.zh: 夏甲又念了一段咒，召来另一个鬼影——这个可不美：砰的一声，一个丑陋的黑色小恶魔出现了，哑着嗓子答了一句，就把一只黑瓶子扔给胡戈，嘲笑着不见了。

ex.t: I see him now, it is that imp Tina who makes me a fool with my cap.
ex.zh: 我现在明白了，是那个小鬼蒂娜拿我的帽子出我的丑。

ex.zh: 怎么，这会儿这只锡壶又满上了，要不是你这圣维特斯的小鬼——滚开，你这哆嗦病！

ex.zh: 佩罗一声咒骂，棍子打在一副瘦骨上的闷响，一声尖锐的痛叫——地狱开了门。

ex.zh: 他什么也感觉不到了，只是极模糊地听见棒子砸在身上的声音。

ex.zh: 可在鲸身上，这两扇窗框是分开装上的，成了两扇各自独立的窗，只是把视野糟蹋得厉害。

ex.zh: 真正的力量从不损害美与和谐，倒常常赋予它们；在一切雄伟之美的事物里，力量都跟那魔力大有关系。

senses.d: the act of piercing with a sharpened stake as a form of punishment or torture

ex.t: It may be burial alive, or death by fire, or by drowning, or by impalement, or fifty other deaths.
ex.zh: 可能是活埋，可能是烧死、淹死、穿刺，或者另外五十种死法。

senses.d: pierce with a sharp stake or point
x: impale a shrimp on a skewer

senses.d: kill by piercing with a spear or sharp pole

ex.zh: 他一把抓住信，抓起艇上的小刀，把信戳在刀尖上，就这样“装着货”送回船上。

ex.zh: 你若把它撬起来顶在头上，露出那一排排的牙，它就像一道可怕的闸门；唉，对捕鲸业中许多可怜虫来说，它确实就是闸门——那些尖齿带着穿刺之力朝他们落下来。

senses.d: incapable of being perceived by the senses especially the sense of touch- James Jeans

senses.d: imperceptible to the senses or the mind

impalpable shadows

senses.d: not perceptible to the touch

ex.t: If this be so, fancy the irresistibleness of that might, to which the most impalpable and destructive of all elements contributes.
ex.zh: 倘若果真如此，那就想想那股力量何等不可抗拒吧——一切元素中最不可捉摸、也最具破坏性的那一种，也来助它一臂之力。

ex.zh: 普罗斯小姐的友谊是十足讲实用的那一类，她曾把索霍和邻近的地界搜刮了个遍，寻找穷困的法国人——那些人被先令和半克朗引诱，就肯把烹饪的秘诀传授给她。

ex.zh: 伊丽莎白立刻认出那号衣，猜到是怎么回事，便告诉舅舅、舅母她料想有这份荣幸，叫他们大吃一惊。

x: the cold neutrality of an impartial judge

senses.d: free from undue bias or preconceived opinions
x: an unprejudiced appraisal of the pros and cons
the impartial eye of a scientist

ex.t: It will be a great help to have cool, impartial persons take a look at it, and tell me what they think of it.”
ex.zh: 要能有几个冷静、不偏心的人看一看，告诉我他们怎么看，那是大帮忙。”

ex.t: Here then, from three impartial witnesses, I had a deliberate statement of the entire case.
ex.zh: 于是我就在这儿，从三个不偏不倚的证人那里，得到了对这整个案子的慎重陈述。

ex.t: It is impossible for me to be impartial.
ex.zh: 要我毫无偏私，是办不到的。

senses.d: an inclination to weigh both views or opinions equally

ex.t: “Serious objections,” remarked the Provincial Mayor, with an air of impartiality, turning towards the Time Traveller.
ex.zh: “很严重的异议，”省长带着公正的神气说，同时转向时间旅行者。

senses.d: transmit (knowledge or skills)
x: give a secret to the Russians
leave your name and address here

senses.d: bestow a quality on
x: Her presence lends a certain cachet to the company
The music added a lot to the play

senses.d: transmit or serve as the medium for transmission
x: Sound carries well over water
The airwaves carry the sound

ex.t: That ghastly whiteness it is which imparts such an abhorrent mildness, even more loathsome than terrific, to the dumb gloating of their aspect.
ex.zh: 正是那惨白的白，才给它们那无声的贪馋神色，添上了那样一种可憎的温和——比可怕还要令人厌恶。

ex.t: This triune structure, as much as anything else, imparts power to the tail.
ex.zh: 这三位一体的构造，跟别的任何东西一样，把力量给了这尾巴。

senses.d: incapable of being passed

ex.t: “My last supplication of all, is this; and with it, I will relieve you of a visitor with whom I well know you have nothing in unison, and between whom and you there is an impassable space.
ex.zh: “我最后一个请求是这个；说完这句话，我就替你打发走一个客人——我很清楚你跟他毫无共鸣，你和他之间隔着一道走不过去的距离。

ex.t: Not, however, from any fear of disadvantage from it individually to herself; for at any rate there seemed a gulf impassable between them.
ex.zh: 不过，她倒不是怕这事单独对她自己有什么不利；因为无论如何，他们之间似乎已经隔着一道过不去的深沟。

ex.t: “Yet if the lady is correct in saying that the flooring and walls are sound, and that the door, window, and chimney are impassable, then her sister must have been undoubtedly alone when she met her mysterious end.”
ex.zh: “可要是这位女士说得不错——地板和墙壁都完好，门窗和烟囱都进不去人——那么她姐姐遭遇那桩神秘死亡时，必定是独自一人。”

senses.d: characterized by intense emotion
x: ardent love
an ardent lover

ex.t: Marilla’s impassioned grief, breaking all the bounds of natural reserve and lifelong habit in its stormy rush, she could comprehend better than Anne’s tearless agony.
ex.zh: 玛丽拉那场痛哭，冲破了她天性的含蓄和一辈子的习惯，来势如暴风；这个黛安娜倒比较能懂，胜过懂安妮那无泪的痛。

ex.t: A subdued impassioned murmur was audible in the room beyond, and Miss Baker leaned forward unashamed, trying to hear.
ex.zh: 隔壁房间里传来一阵压低了的、激昂的低语，贝克小姐毫不遮掩地向前倾身，想听个清楚。

ex.t: Some time toward midnight Tom Buchanan and Mrs. Wilson stood face to face discussing, in impassioned voices, whether Mrs. Wilson had any right to mention Daisy's name.
ex.zh: 快到午夜时，汤姆·布坎南和威尔逊太太面对面站着，激烈地争论威尔逊太太到底有没有权利提黛西的名字。

senses.d: having or revealing little emotion or sensibility; not easily aroused or excited- Nordhoff & Hall-Virginia Woolf
x: her impassive remoteness
he remained impassive, showing neither interest in nor concern for our plight

senses.d: deliberately impassive in manner
x: deadpan humor
his face remained expressionless as the verdict was read

ex.t: Impassive faces, yet with a suspended--not an abolished--expression on them; faces, rather, in a fearful pause, as having yet to raise the dropped lids of the eyes, and bear witness with the bloodless lips, “THOU DIDST IT!”
ex.zh: 那是没有表情的脸，可脸上有一种悬着的——不是取消了的——表情；不如说，那是停在可怕停顿里的脸，仿佛还要抬起垂下的眼皮，用没有血色的嘴唇作证：“这是你干的！”

ex.t: Madame Defarge met the lifted eyebrows and forehead with a cold, impassive stare.
ex.zh: 德法热太太迎着那扬起的眉毛和额头，冷冷地、毫无表情地凝视。

ex.t: Of the riders in the tumbrils, some observe these things, and all things on their last roadside, with an impassive stare; others, with a lingering interest in the ways of life and men.
ex.zh: 死囚车里的人，有的带着无动于衷的凝视，看着这些，看着他们最后一段路旁的一切；有的还对人生和人的行径留着一点余兴。

senses.d: in an impassive manner
x: he submitted impassively to his arrest

ex.t: 'Martin is one of us,' said O'Brien impassively.
ex.zh: “马丁是我们的人，”奥布莱恩不动声色地说。

senses.d: a lack of patience; irritation with anything that causes delay
a restless desire for change and excitement
a dislike of anything that causes delay

ex.t: My mother pulled it up with impatience, and there lay before us, the last things in the chest, a bundle tied up in oilcloth, and looking like papers, and a canvas bag that gave forth, at a touch, the jingle of gold.
He was not prone to rashness and precipitate action; and in the bitter hatred between him and Spitz he betrayed no impatience, shunned all offensive acts.
With an exclamation of impatience, but with his unchangeable face, Monseigneur looked out.
ex.zh: 爵爷带着一声不耐烦的啧声向外看，脸却一点没变。

senses.d: restless or short-tempered under delay or opposition
x: impatient with the slower students
impatient of criticism

senses.d: (usually followed by `to') full of eagerness
x: impatient to begin
raring to go

ex.t: I am too ardent in execution and too impatient of difficulties.
But he is generally melancholy and despairing, and sometimes he gnashes his teeth, as if impatient of the weight of woes that oppresses him.
“The brothers were waiting in a room down-stairs, impatient to ride away.
ex.zh: “两兄弟在楼下的一间屋里等着，急着骑马走。

senses.d: with impatience; in an impatient manner
x: he answered her impatiently

ex.t: He drew my head back and fixed the rein so tight that it was almost intolerable; then he went to Ginger, who was impatiently jerking her head up and down against the bit, as was her way now.
I gave a loud, shrill neigh for help; again and again I neighed, pawing the ground impatiently, and tossing my head to get the rein loose.
she said impatiently.

ex.t: She will be in a state of mind to impeach the justice of the Republic.
ex.zh: 她那心境，会去非难共和国的公道。

ex.t: Here are three instances, then, which I personally know the truth of; but I have heard of many other instances from persons whose veracity in the matter there is no good ground to impeach.
ex.zh: 那么，这里就是三个我亲自知道其真实的例子；可我还从别人那里听说过许多别的例子，那些人在此事上的诚实，没有良好的理由可以怀疑。

senses.d: challenge the honesty or veracity of

ex.t: The peddler had certainly spoken the truth when he declared that the dye wouldn’t wash off, however his veracity might be impeached in other respects.
ex.zh: 小贩说这染料洗不掉，这话倒是真的，尽管他在别的方面未必老实。

senses.d: a formal document charging a public official with misconduct in office

ex.t: A blush on the countenance of Monsieur the Marquis was no impeachment of his high breeding; it was not from within; it was occasioned by an external circumstance beyond his control--the setting sun.
ex.zh: 侯爵先生脸上的红晕并不损害他高贵的教养；那不是从内里来的；那是由一桩他无法控制的外在情形造成的——落日。

ex.t: Upon which impeachment of what to her was her most essential sex-prerogative, she made their lives unendurable.
ex.zh: 这等于攻击她身上最要紧的女性特权，她就叫他们日子过不下去。

senses.d: be a hindrance or obstacle to
x: She is impeding the progress of our project

senses.d: block passage through

ex.t: In the van, on all fours, is Great Big Little Panther, a brave of so many scalps that in his present position they somewhat impede his progress.

They attached the line with which they had been snubbing the boat to Buck’s neck and shoulders, being careful that it should neither strangle him nor impede his swimming, and launched him into the stream.
ex.zh: 他们把先前系船的那根绳拴在巴克的脖子和肩膀上，小心不勒住他、不碍他游水，然后把他放进河里。

senses.d: something immaterial that interferes with or delays action or progress
any structure that makes progress difficult

ex.t: I had gazed upon the fortifications and impediments that seemed to keep human beings from entering the citadel of nature, and rashly and ignorantly I had repined.
And, sir, if business imposes its restraints and its silences and impediments, Mr. Darnay as a young gentleman of generosity knows how to make allowance for that circumstance.
ex.zh: 而且，先生，事务要是加给人一些约束、沉默和阻碍，达尔内先生作为一位宽厚的年轻绅士，是懂得体谅这种情况的。

senses.d: urged or forced to action through moral pressure
x: felt impelled to take a stand against the issue

ex.t: Impelled by a laudable ambition to study the art and mystery of his father’s honest calling, Young Jerry, keeping as close to house fronts, walls, and doorways, as his eyes were close to one another, held his honoured parent in view.
ex.zh: 小杰里被一种可赞的雄心催着，要去研究他父亲那诚实行当的技艺和奥秘；他紧贴着人家的门面、墙和门洞，紧得就像他两只眼睛挨在一起，一路盯着他那可敬的父亲。

ex.t: He imitated the action of a man’s being impelled forward by the butt-ends of muskets.
ex.zh: 他模仿一个人被枪托往前推的动作。

ex.t: I did not dare return to the apartment which I inhabited, but felt impelled to hurry on, although drenched by the rain which poured from a black and comfortless sky.
ex.zh: 我不敢回到我住的那套房间去，只觉得被逼着往前赶，尽管黑色的、毫无慰藉的天空泼下的雨把我淋透了。

senses.d: markedly effective as if by emotional pressure
x: impelling skill as a teller of tales
an impelling personality

ex.t: Since I knew you, I have been troubled by a remorse that I thought would never reproach me again, and have heard whispers from old voices impelling me upward, that I thought were silent for ever.
ex.zh: 自从认识你，我就被一种我以为再也不会来责备我的悔恨搅扰，又听见一些我以为永远沉默了的旧声音在低语，催我向上。

senses.d: be imminent or about to happen
x: Changes are impending

ex.t: I was bound by a solemn promise which I had not yet fulfilled and dared not break, or if I did, what manifold miseries might not impend over me and my devoted family!
ex.zh: 我被一个庄重的诺言绑着，那诺言我还没履行，也不敢打破；若我打破了，多少种苦不会临到我和我挚爱的家人头上！

senses.d: be imminent or about to happen
x: Changes are impending

ex.t: But, an affectionate glance at his wife, so happy and busy, made him resolute not to tell her what impended (he had been half moved to do it, so strange it was to him to act in anything without her quiet aid), and the day passed quickly.
ex.zh: 可是，他深情地看一眼他那般幸福、那般忙碌的妻子，便下定决心不把逼近的事告诉她（他本来已有些动心想说，因为做任何事没有她静静的帮助，在他都觉得那么不惯），于是一天很快就过去了。

senses.d: close in time; about to occur
x: retribution is at hand
some people believe the day of judgment is close at hand

ex.t: Only Spitz quivered and bristled as he staggered back and forth, snarling with horrible menace, as though to frighten off impending death.

Hence Monseigneur had taken his sister from a convent, while there was yet time to ward off the impending veil, the cheapest garment she could wear, and had bestowed her as a prize upon a very rich Farmer-General, poor in family.
ex.zh: 因此，爵爷趁还来得及挡住那即将落到她头上的面纱——那是她能穿的最便宜的一件衣裳——的时候，把他妹妹从修道院里接了出来，把她当作奖品赐给了一个很有钱、出身却很寒微的包税人。

ex.t: From this time Felix was more employed, and the heart-moving indications of impending famine disappeared.
ex.zh: 从这时起费利克斯更忙了，那叫人心碎的饥荒征兆也消失了。

senses.d: not admitting of penetration or passage into or through

impenetrable rain forests

senses.d: permitting little if any light to pass through because of denseness of matter
x: dense smoke
heavy fog

senses.d: impossible to understand
x: impenetrable jargon

ex.t: Living, as they did, in what appeared to me impenetrable darkness, their eyes were abnormally large and sensitive, just as are the pupils of the abysmal fishes, and they reflected the light in the same way.
It was not in impenetrable shadow as the other objects in the yard were, but had a dismal light about it, like a bad lobster in a dark cellar.
ex.zh: 它不像院子里别的东西那样陷在穿不透的暗影里，倒有一层幽幽的光，像地窖暗处一只坏掉的龙虾。

ex.t:
When she came to the lines

The stubborn spearsmen still made good Their dark impenetrable wood,

she stopped in ecstasy to shut her eyes that she might the better fancy herself one of that heroic ring.
ex.zh: 她念到“那些顽强的枪手依旧守住了他们那幽暗难入的矛林”这几句时，欢喜得停下脚，闭上眼睛，好把自己想象成那英雄圈子里的一员。

senses.d: not penitent or remorseful
impervious to moral persuasion

ex.t: He seemed quite used to impenitent Peleg and his ways.
ex.zh: 他仿佛对不肯悔改的佩莱格和他那一套已经很习惯了。

senses.d: a mood that expresses an intention to influence the listener's behavior
requiring attention or action
x: as nuclear weapons proliferate, preventing war becomes imperative
requests that grew more and more imperative

senses.d: some duty that is essential and urgent
relating to verbs in the imperative mood

ex.t: Two or three times, the matter in hand became so knotty, that the jackal found it imperative on him to get up, and steep his towels anew.
ex.zh: 有两三次，手里的材料变得太棘手，豺狗觉得非站起来把毛巾重新浸过不可。

ex.t: It became imperative to lance the flying whale, or be content to lose him.
ex.zh: 那就非给这飞逃的鲸一矛不可，否则只好甘心失掉他。

ex.t: There was imperative need to be constantly alert; for these dogs and men were not town dogs and men.
ex.zh: 必须时时刻刻警醒；因为这些狗和人，都不是城里的狗和人。

senses.d: in an imperative and commanding manner

ex.t: I have resolved every night, when I am not imperatively occupied by my duties, to record, as nearly as possible in his own words, what he has related during the day.

Before I could reply that he was my neighbour dinner was announced; wedging his tense arm imperatively under mine, Tom Buchanan compelled me from the room as though he were moving a checker to another square.
ex.zh: 我还没来得及回答说他是我邻居，开饭就通报了；汤姆·布坎南不容分说地把一条紧绷的胳膊插到我臂下，硬把我带出屋去，像把一枚棋子挪到另一格。

senses.d: impossible or difficult to perceive by the mind or senses
x: an imperceptible drop in temperature
an imperceptible nod

ex.t: In one of these was a small and almost imperceptible chink through which the eye could just penetrate.
ex.zh: 其中一块板上有一道极小、几乎看不出的缝，眼光勉强能穿过去。

ex.t: While the ear of the former has an external opening, that of the latter is entirely and evenly covered over with a membrane, so as to be quite imperceptible from without.
ex.zh: 前者的耳朵有一个朝外的开口，后者的却整个被一层薄膜平平地覆住，从外面完全看不出来。

ex.t: All the old constellations had gone from the sky, however: that slow movement which is imperceptible in a hundred human lifetimes, had long since rearranged them in unfamiliar groupings.
ex.zh: 然而天上的旧星座都已不见：那种在人类百代中也察觉不到的缓慢移动，早已把它们重新排成陌生的组合。

senses.d: in an imperceptible manner or to an imperceptible degree
x: the power of the Secretary of State in London increased gradually but imperceptibly

ex.t: Uncle Scrooge had imperceptibly become so gay and light of heart, that he would have pledged the unconscious company in return, and thanked them in an inaudible speech, if the Ghost had given him time.
“Well, she does it so imperceptibly that I don’t think I shall mind much.
ex.zh: “她管得那么不知不觉，我想我不会太在意。

ex.t: At any rate, Miss Baker's lips fluttered, she nodded at me almost imperceptibly, and then quickly tipped her head back again-the object she was balancing had obviously tottered a little and given her something of a fright.
ex.zh: 不管怎样，贝克小姐的嘴唇动了动，几乎看不出地朝我点了下头，随即又迅速把头仰了回去——她顶着的那样东西显然晃了一下，叫她受了点惊。

senses.d: not perfect; defective or inadequate
x: had only an imperfect understanding of his responsibilities
imperfect mortals

senses.d: wanting in moral strength, courage, or will; having the attributes of man as opposed to e.g. divine beings
x: I'm only a fallible human
frail humanity

senses.d: a tense of verbs used in describing action that is on-going

ex.t: The moral life of man forms part of the subject-matter of the artist, but the morality of art consists in the perfect use of an imperfect medium.

Shortly, this worn-out murderer descried in the imperfect light one of the carriages of Monseigneur, and, staggering to that gorgeous vehicle, climbed in at the door, and shut himself up to take his rest on its dainty cushions.
ex.zh: 不一会儿，这筋疲力尽的凶手在微弱的光里认出大人的一辆马车，便摇摇晃晃走到那华丽的车上，从车门爬进去，把自己关在里面，在那精致的坐垫上歇息。

ex.t: “I am sorry to see a pupil of mine displaying such a temper and such a vindictive spirit,” he said in a solemn tone, as if the mere fact of being a pupil of his ought to root out all evil passions from the hearts of small imperfect mortals.
ex.zh: “我很遗憾，看见我的学生露这样的脾气、这样的报复心，”他语调庄重，仿佛只消是他菲利普斯的学生，就该把渺小而不完美的凡人心中一切恶念连根拔除似的。

senses.d: the state or an instance of being imperfect

ex.t: The power of doing anything with quickness is always much prized by the possessor, and often without any attention to the imperfection of the performance.
ex.zh: 做事快的能力，总被拥有它的人看得极重，往往还不顾事情做得多不完美。

senses.d: in an imperfect or faulty way- Jane Austen
x: The lobe was imperfectly developed
Miss Bennet would not play at all amiss if she practiced more

ex.t: But I felt it; and it did not disincline me towards him; though I felt impatience at what seemed like mystery in him, so imperfectly as he was known to me then.
ex.zh: 但我感到了它；它并没有叫我不愿亲近他；只是他身上的那种神秘——他当时在我眼里还是那样模糊不全——叫我有点不耐烦。

ex.t: Suddenly he began writing in sheer panic, only imperfectly aware of what he was setting down.
ex.zh: 他突然在纯粹的恐慌中写起来，对自己写下的东西只是一知半解。

ex.t: History had already been rewritten, but fragments of the literature of the past survived here and there, imperfectly censored, and so long as one retained one's knowledge of Oldspeak it was possible to read them.
ex.zh: 历史早已被重写，但过去文学的残片仍零散地留存下来，审查得不彻底；只要人还保有旧话的知识，就有可能读懂它们。

senses.d: relating to or associated with an empire

the imperial gallon was standardized legally throughout the British Empire

senses.d: of or belonging to the British Imperial System of weights and measures
befitting or belonging to an emperor or empress
x: imperial palace

senses.d: belonging to or befitting a supreme ruler
x: golden age of imperial splendor
purple tyrant

senses.d: a small tufted beard worn by Emperor Napoleon III
a piece of luggage carried on top of a coach

ex.t: Prima donna Imperial Opera of Warsaw-yes!
I’ve seen the imperial family several times, the emperor an ugly, hard-looking man, the empress pale and pretty, but dressed in bad taste, I thought—purple dress, green hat, and yellow gloves.
ex.zh: 我见过皇室好几次：皇帝是个丑陋、冷硬的男人；皇后苍白而美丽，可我觉得她穿得没品味——紫衣裳、绿帽子、黄手套。

ex.t: Whaling is imperial!
ex.zh: 捕鲸是帝王的行当！

senses.d: a believer in imperialism
of or relating to imperialism
x: imperialistic wars

ex.t: A lot of Imperialist ladies asked me to tea to meet schoolmasters from New Zealand and editors from Vancouver, and that was the dismalest business of all.
ex.zh: 许多帝国主义派的太太请我喝茶，去见新西兰的校长和温哥华的编辑，那是最乏味的事。

senses.d: pose a threat to; present a danger to
x: The pollution is endangering the crops

ex.zh: 营业时间一到，洛里先生那生意人的脑子里浮起的第一批考虑之一就是：他没有权利把一个流亡囚犯的妻子藏在银行屋顶下，让特尔森担风险。

senses.d: pose a threat to; present a danger to
x: The pollution is endangering the crops

ex.zh: 这项对旧例的改良，不是别人，正是斯塔布引进的；为的是给那身处险境的镖手一个尽可能有力的保证，担保他这牵索人忠实而警觉。

ex.t: “You have already imperilled the whole success of our expedition.
ex.zh: “你这一下已经把咱们这次行动的成功整个置于险境了。

senses.d: having or showing arrogant superiority to and disdain of those one views as unworthy- W.L.Shirer
x: some economists are disdainful of their colleagues in other social disciplines
haughty aristocrats

If our impulses were confined to hunger, thirst, and desire, we might be nearly free; but now we are moved by every wind that blows and a chance word or scene that that word may convey to us.

ex.zh:
安妮这一时冲动的亲热叫她暗自欢喜得很，这大概正是她粗声粗气开口的缘故：

ex.zh: “不过当然，”她说，“我尽可以问心无愧地走进他那郡，拿几块石化了的晶石走，他也不会发觉我。”

ex.zh: 这番劝告虽好，对我的情形却全然用不上；若不是悔恨把它的苦味、恐怖把它的惊惶掺进我别的感觉里，我本该是头一个藏起自己的悲伤去安慰亲友的人。

ex.t: This is he; this helpless, inarticulately murmuring, wandering old man pointed out.
ex.zh: 这就是他；有人指出这个无助的、含混低语着、神志游移的老人。

senses.d: lack of attention

ex.t: Hurst called them to order, with bitter complaints of their inattention to what was going forward.
From his complete inattention to the tidings, you would think that moody Ahab had not heard his menial.
ex.zh: 看他听见这消息时全然不留心的样子，你会以为沉郁的亚哈根本没听见这仆役的话。

ex.t: She endeavoured to persuade herself that she did not regret it; but she could no longer be blind to Miss Bingley’s inattention.
ex.zh: 她竭力叫自己相信并不为此惋惜；可对宾利小姐的冷淡，她不能再装作看不见了。

senses.d: showing a lack of attention or care
x: inattentive students
an inattentive babysitter

senses.d: not showing due care or attention
x: inattentive students
an inattentive babysitter

ex.t: “I never saw a more promising inclination; he was growing quite inattentive to other people, and wholly engrossed by her.
ex.zh: “我从没见过比这更有指望的情意；他渐渐对别人全然不留心，一颗心全在她身上。

ex.t: Demades the orator was once speaking in the Assembly at Athens; but the people were very inattentive to what he was saying, so he stopped and said, "Gentlemen, I should like to tell you one of Æsop's fables."
ex.zh: 演说家德马德斯有一次在雅典公民大会上讲话，众人却全不留心听，他便停下来，说：“诸位，我想给你们讲一则伊索寓言。”

senses.d: impossible to hear; imperceptible by the ear
x: an inaudible conversation

ex.t: Uncle Scrooge had imperceptibly become so gay and light of heart, that he would have pledged the unconscious company in return, and thanked them in an inaudible speech, if the Ghost had given him time.

May’s answer was inaudible, but another young lady, whose temper was evidently a little soured by making lemonade, added, with a disagreeable laugh, “Very lovely, for she knew she wouldn’t sell them at her own table.”
ex.zh: 梅的回答听不见，可另一位年轻小姐——她的脾气显然是被做柠檬水弄酸了的——带着难听的笑补了一句：“漂亮得很，因为她知道自己摊子上卖不出去。”

ex.t: The spoken words that are inaudible among the flying spindles; those same words are plainly heard without the walls, bursting from the opened casements.
ex.zh: 在飞转的纺锤之间听不见的说话声，那些同样的话在墙外却听得清清楚楚，从敞开的窗子里迸出来。

senses.d: in an inaudible manner
x: she spoke inaudibly low

ex.t: That’s a useful accomplishment, which no woman should be without,” said Mrs. March, laughing inaudibly at the recollection of Jo’s dinner party, for she had met Miss Crocker and heard her account of it.
ex.zh: 这是一样本事，女人个个都该会。”马奇太太说，想起乔那顿请客，不出声地笑了——她碰上过克罗克小姐，听她讲了。

ex.t: Winston sighed inaudibly.
ex.zh: 温斯顿无声地叹了口气。

ex.t: “You will never hear the tom-tom again,” he muttered, but inaudibly of course, for strict silence had been enjoined.
ex.zh: “你再也不会听见手鼓响了。”他嘟囔道，当然没人听得见，因为严令不许作声。

ex.zh: 我把它们收进船里么？”

ex.t: The jibs behind me cracked aloud, the rudder slammed to, the whole ship gave a sickening heave and shudder, and at the same moment the main-boom swung inboard, the sheet groaning in the blocks, and showed me the lee after-deck.
ex.zh: 我背后的几张前帆啪啪大响，舵砰地一下打满，整条船叫人恶心地一抬一抖；同时主帆杠摆了进来，帆索在滑轮里吱嘎作响，把背风的后甲板露给了我。

senses.d: present at birth but not necessarily hereditary; acquired during fetal development

ex.zh: 可乔西·派伊虽然缺少些讨人喜欢的品性，走栅栏这一手倒是天生就会，又练得纯熟。

senses.d: not able to be computed or enumerated
too much to be measured
x: untold suffering
incalculable riches

ex.t: I have endured incalculable fatigue, and cold, and hunger; do you dare destroy my hopes?”
ex.zh: 我受了算不清的疲乏、寒冷和饥饿；你敢毁掉我的希望吗？”

ex.t: What would happen now in the dim, incalculable hours?
ex.zh: 在那些幽暗的、无从计算的时辰里，会发生什么？

senses.d: emitting light as a result of being heated
x: an incandescent bulb

senses.d: characterized by ardent emotion or intensity or brilliance
x: an incandescent performance

senses.d: a ritual recitation of words or sounds believed to have a magical effect

ex.t: Hagar, the witch, chanted an awful incantation over her kettleful of simmering toads, with weird effect.
ex.zh: 女巫夏甲对着一锅咕嘟咕嘟的癞蛤蟆念起可怕的咒语，效果古怪得很。

ex.t: So still and subdued and yet somehow preluding was all the scene, and such an incantation of reverie lurked in the air, that each silent sailor seemed resolved into his own invisible self.
ex.zh: 整个场景那么静、那么低沉，却又不知怎的像是前奏，空气里潜伏着那样一种沉思的咒语，以致每个沉默的水手都仿佛溶化进了他自己那看不见的自身。

senses.d: (followed by `of') lacking capacity or ability
x: incapable of carrying a tune

senses.d: not being susceptible to or admitting of something (usually followed by `of')
x: incapable of solution

senses.d: (followed by `of') not having the temperament or inclination for
x: simply incapable of lying

senses.d: not meeting requirements
x: unequal to the demands put upon him

ex.t: I will not admit that one speech or one action of this inestimable man is incapable of being reconciled with reality, and I should not wonder if many of these words and actions are historically true.
Now, you know me; you know I am incapable of all the higher and better flights of men.
ex.zh: 现在，你了解我；你知道我这个人，做不出人家那些更高更美的飞腾。

ex.t: He was quite incapable of any compassionate feeling about the boy, or about his fate.
ex.zh: 他对那男孩、对他的命运，全然没有半点慈悲之感。

senses.d: lacking in or deprived of strength or power

helpless with laughter

ex.t: Or, if for any reason thought to be corporeally incapacitated for that, yet such an one would seem superlatively competent to cheer and howl on his underlings to the attack.
ex.zh: 或者，若因什么缘故被认为肉体上已不能胜任此事，这样的人似乎也优异无比，足以在他的下属身边鼓劲、嚎叫，催他们进攻。

senses.d: lock up or confine, in or as in a jail

ex.zh: 萨格港（人家就这么叫他）对这位先知的事不肯相信，还举出另一个理由，隐约是关乎他那被囚的躯体与鲸的胃液。

senses.d: make concrete and real
possessing or existing in bodily form- Shakespeare
x: what seemed corporal melted as breath into the wind
an incarnate spirit

senses.d: represent in bodily form
x: He embodies all that is evil wrong with the system
The painting substantiates the feelings of the artist

senses.d: invested with a bodily form especially of a human body
x: a monarch...regarded as a god incarnate

ex.t: That certain sultanism of his brain, which had otherwise in a good degree remained unmanifested; through those forms that same sultanism became incarnate in an irresistible dictatorship.
ex.zh: 他脑子里那种苏丹式的独断，本来在很大程度上一直不曾显露；借着这些礼数，那同样的独断便化成了肉身，成了一种不可抗拒的专制。

ex.t: He was a devil incarnate.
ex.zh: 他是个魔鬼化身。

ex.t: And truly Buck was the Fiend incarnate, raging at their heels and dragging them down like deer as they raced through the trees.
ex.zh: 巴克真就是恶鬼化身，在他们脚后发狂，他们穿林奔逃时，他像撂鹿一样把他们撂倒。

senses.d: time passed in a particular bodily form

ex.zh: 白鲸在他面前游着，成了那些恶毒力量的偏执狂式的化身——那些力量，一些深沉的人觉得在自己体内啃噬，直到他们只剩半颗心、半叶肺地活着。

ex.t: The Hindoo whale referred to, occurs in a separate department of the wall, depicting the incarnation of Vishnu in the form of leviathan, learnedly known as the Matse Avatar.
ex.zh: 所说的那头印度鲸，出现在墙面另一处，描绘毗湿奴化身为巨鲸，学界称之为摩蹉化身。

ex.t: At his lips' touch she blossomed for him like a flower and the incarnation was complete.
ex.zh: 他的嘴唇一触，她就像一朵花似的为他绽放，道成肉身就此完成。

ex.t: He took a cigarette from a crumpled packet marked VICTORY CIGARETTES and incautiously held it upright, whereupon the tobacco fell out on to the floor.
ex.zh: 他从一包压皱的烟里抽出一支，烟盒上印着：胜利香烟。他没留神把烟竖着拿，烟丝就掉到了地上。

ex.t: His behaviour to herself could now have had no tolerable motive: he had either been deceived with regard to her fortune, or had been gratifying his vanity by encouraging the preference which she believed she had most incautiously shown.
ex.zh: 他待她自己的那番举动，如今看来也没有一个说得过去的动机：他不是对她的家产会错了意，就是借鼓励她的偏爱来满足虚荣——而那份偏爱，她相信是自己极其不慎地露出来的。

senses.d: a substance that produces a fragrant odor when burned
perfume especially with a censer
the pleasing scent produced when incense is burned
x: incense filled the room

senses.d: make furious

ex.t: The sight of these poor revellers appeared to interest the Spirit very much, for he stood with Scrooge beside him in a baker's doorway, and taking off the covers as their bearers passed, sprinkled incense on their dinners from his torch.
ex.zh: 这些穷开心的景象似乎叫精灵很感兴趣：他带着斯克鲁奇站在一家面包房门口，趁提饭的人走过，揭开盖子，用火炬往他们的饭菜上洒了些香。

ex.t: I meant not to incense thee.
ex.zh: 我并非有意激你。

ex.t: The heavy odour of incense seemed to cling about its pages and to trouble the brain.
ex.zh: 浓郁的熏香气味仿佛附在书页上，搅得人头脑发昏。

ex.t: Her Ladyship was highly incensed.
ex.zh: 夫人气极了。

ex.t: My friends, then, were still alive, and though I partly believed the truth of Silver’s statement, that the cabin party were incensed at me for my desertion, I was more relieved than distressed by what I heard.
ex.zh: 那么我的朋友们还活着；虽然我有点相信西尔弗的话是真的，就是说舱里的人因为我擅自离开而恼我，可我听了这些，与其说难过，不如说松了口气。

senses.d: uninterrupted in time and indefinitely long continuing
x: the ceaseless thunder of surf
in constant pain

ex.t: Incessant torture of remorse."
ex.zh: 只有悔恨无休无止的折磨。”

ex.t: "Oh! captive, bound, and double-ironed," cried the phantom, "not to know, that ages of incessant labour by immortal creatures, for this earth must pass into eternity before the good of which it is susceptible is all developed.
ex.zh: “啊！被囚的、被缚的、戴着双重镣铐的，”幽灵叫道，“竟不知道：不朽的生灵为这尘世所付出的无穷世代的劳作，非得一直延续到永恒，这尘世所能承受的善才全都会生发出来。

ex.t: The footsteps were incessant, and the hurry of them became more and more rapid.
ex.zh: 脚步声不停，那匆忙越来越快。

x: dance inspires him ceaselessly to strive higher and higher toward the shining pinnacle of perfection that is the goal of every artiste

senses.d: without interruption
x: the world is constantly changing

ex.t: I couldn't sleep all night; a foghorn was groaning incessantly on the Sound, and I tossed half-sick between grotesque reality and savage, frightening dreams.
The position appeared by no means to please him, however, with an increasing rabble surrounding the coach, deriding him, making grimaces at him, and incessantly groaning and calling out: “Yah!
ex.zh: 可这身份似乎一点也不叫他受用：越来越多的乱民围着马车，嘲弄他，朝他做鬼脸，不停地哼哼着喊：“呸！

ex.t: All this time it was incessantly hopping on behind and gaining on him, so that when the boy got to his own door he had reason for being half dead.
ex.zh: 这工夫它一刻不停地在他身后蹦着，越追越近，所以那孩子跑到自家门口时，有理由半死不活。

a unit of measurement for advertising space
advance slowly, as if by inches
x: He edged towards the car

ex.t: For what seemed ages piled on ages, I lay there, frozen with the most awful fears, not daring to drag away my hand; yet ever thinking that if I could but stir it one single inch, the horrid spell would be broken.
The same cautious counsel directed every step that lay before him, and had prepared every inch of his road.
ex.zh: 同样是那谨慎的劝告，指引着他前面的每一步，把他路上的每一寸都预备好了。

ex.t: Miss Pross had nothing beautiful about her; years had not tamed the wildness, or softened the grimness, of her appearance; but, she too was a determined woman in her different way, and she measured Madame Defarge with her eyes, every inch.
ex.zh: 普罗斯小姐身上没有好看的地方；岁月没有驯服她外貌的野气，也没有磨软那严厉；可她也以她不同的方式是个坚决的女人，她用眼睛一寸一寸地量着德法热太太。

But she went on all the same, shedding gallons of tears, until there was a large pool all round her, about four inches deep and reaching half down the hall.

ex.zh: 一句故意抛出的、顺带提到星期几和几号的话，引得他思索、计算，显然使他不安。

ex.zh: 他说话时做出种种手势，仿佛顺便模仿他从未见过的那许多信号里的少数几个。

ex.t: Hence, in the English, this thing of whaling good cheer is not normal and natural, but incidental and particular; and, therefore, must have some special origin, which is here pointed out, and will be still further elucidated.
ex.zh: 因此，在英国人身上，捕鲸船这种好伙食并非正常自然的，而是偶发的、特殊的；所以必定有某种特别的来源，这里就指出来，下面还要进一步阐明。

ex.t: As I walked away, I was full of thoughtfulness; what had been incidentally revealed to me of Captain Ahab, filled me with a certain wild vagueness of painfulness concerning him.
ex.zh: 我走开的时候，满心都是思量；人家这样顺便透露给我的关于亚哈船长的事，叫我对他生出一种说不出的、狂野而模糊的难受。

ex.t: Nor, will the tragic dramatist who would depict mortal indomitableness in its fullest sweep and direct swing, ever forget a hint, incidentally so important in his art, as the one now alluded to.
ex.zh: 那位想把人间的不可屈服，在其最饱满的铺展与最直截的挥击中刻画出来的悲剧家，也绝不会忘掉刚才提到的这一类暗示——它在他的艺术里，碰巧极为要紧。

ex.t: This peculiarity is strikingly evinced in the head, as in some part of this book will be incidentally shown.
ex.zh: 这一特点在头部表现得尤为触目，本书某处将会顺带说明。

ex.zh: 往后若再有新的情况可记，我会隔些时候续写关于这陌生人的日记。

ex.zh: 客人带着几分明显的惊讶，瞥了一眼这个懒散倚坐的人——别人向他描述的，无疑正是全欧洲最犀利、最干练的推理家与代理人。

ex.zh: 我问——对我朋友这种锋利的推理，我一向极感兴趣。

ex.zh: “对谁都失礼，不正是爱情的精髓吗？”

ex.zh: 我若失礼，这难道不算一点可以原谅的理由？

x: the growing inequality between rich and poor

ex.t: We watched the rapid progress of the traveller with our telescopes until he was lost among the distant inequalities of the ice.
I exchanged my land-sledge for one fashioned for the inequalities of the Frozen Ocean, and purchasing a plentiful stock of provisions, I departed from land.
ex.zh: 我把陆上的雪橇换成一副适于冰海崎岖的，又买足了食物，就离了陆地。

ex.t: “But before the balloons, save for spasmodic jumping and the inequalities of the surface, man had no freedom of vertical movement.”
ex.zh: “可是在气球出现之前，除了偶尔跳一跳、借地势起伏之外，人在垂直方向上并没有移动的自由。”

senses.d: lack of equality
x: the growing inequality between rich and poor

ex.t: From the moment when the machine first made its appearance it was clear to all thinking people that the need for human drudgery, and therefore to a great extent for human inequality, had disappeared.
ex.zh: 从机器刚一出现的那一刻起，一切有思想的人都清楚：对人做苦役的需要，因而在很大程度上对人不平等的需要，已经消失了。

ex.t: There then rose schools of thinkers who interpreted history as a cyclical process and claimed to show that inequality was the unalterable law of human life.
ex.zh: 于是兴起了一些思想流派，把历史解释为循环过程，并声称证明了不平等是人类生活不可更改的规律。

ex.t: The new movements which appeared in the middle years of the century, Ingsoc in Oceania, Neo-Bolshevism in Eurasia, Death-Worship, as it is commonly called, in Eastasia, had the conscious aim of perpetuating UNfreedom and INequality.
ex.zh: 本世纪中叶出现的新运动——大洋国的英社、欧亚国的新布尔什维克主义、东亚国通常所称的崇死——有意识地以永久维持不自由和不平等为目标。

senses.d: unable to move or resist motion
having only a limited ability to react chemically; chemically inactive
x: inert matter
an indifferent chemical in a reaction

senses.d: slow and apathetic
x: she was fat and inert
a sluggish worker

ex.t: She had never seen Marilla sit limply inert like that.
ex.zh: 她从没见过玛丽拉这样软软地、一动不动地坐着。

ex.t: For the first time in his life he did not despise the proles or think of them merely as an inert force which would one day spring to life and regenerate the world.
ex.zh: 他这辈子头一回不鄙视无产者，也不把他们仅仅看成一股惰性的力量，有朝一日会奋起，让世界重生。

senses.d: a disposition to remain inactive or inert
x: he had to overcome his inertia and get back to work

senses.d: (physics) the tendency of a body to maintain its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force

ex.t: He thought with a kind of astonishment of the biological uselessness of pain and fear, the treachery of the human body which always freezes into inertia at exactly the moment when a special effort is needed.
ex.zh: 他带着一种惊异想到，疼痛和恐惧在生物学上多么无用，人体多么背信：恰恰在需要特别使劲的那一刻，它总是僵成死寂。

senses.d: not basic or fundamental
not absolutely necessary
anything that is not essential
x: they discarded all their inessentials

ex.t: And as the moon rose higher the inessential houses began to melt away until gradually I became aware of the old island here that flowered once for Dutch sailors' eyes-a fresh, green breast of the new world.
ex.zh: 月亮越升越高，那些无关紧要的房子开始消融，直到我渐渐意识到这里这座古老的岛——它曾为荷兰水手的眼睛开花——那是新世界一片新鲜、碧绿的胸脯。

senses.d: beyond calculation or measure
x: an incomputable amount
jewels of inestimable value

ex.t: I will not admit that one speech or one action of this inestimable man is incapable of being reconciled with reality, and I should not wonder if many of these words and actions are historically true.
Just so with the head; but with this difference: about the head this envelope, though not so thick, is of a boneless toughness, inestimable by any man who has not handled it.
ex.zh: 头部也是这样；不过有一处不同：包在头上的这层东西虽不那么厚，却有一种无骨的坚韧，没亲手摸过的人是估量不出的。

ex.t: I could not endure the sight; could not possibly fly his howlings; all comfort, sleep itself, inestimable reason would leave me on the long intolerable voyage.
ex.zh: 那样的景象我受不了；他的嚎叫我也躲不开；在这漫长难熬的航程里，一切安慰，连睡眠本身、那无价的理智，都会离开我。

senses.d: the quality of being unavoidable

ex.t: It always happens so in this vale of tears, there is an inevitability about such things which we can only wonder at, deplore, and bear as we best can.
ex.zh: 在这泪谷里事情总是这样；这类事有一种躲不开的必然，我们只能诧异、叹惜，尽力忍受。

senses.d: incapable of being avoided or prevented
x: the inevitable result

senses.d: invariably occurring or appearing
x: the inevitable changes of the seasons

senses.d: an unavoidable event
x: don't argue with the inevitable

ex.t: Gatsby asked me to wait until he was free, and I lingered in the garden until the inevitable swimming party had run up, chilled and exalted, from the black beach, until the lights were extinguished in the guestrooms overhead.

Then she yielded to the inevitable and said tartly:

“Very well, she can go, since nothing else ‘ll please you.”
ex.zh:
随后她向无可奈何低了头，尖刻地说：

“好吧，让她去，反正别的也不能叫你满意。”

ex.t: If the monster executed his threat, death was inevitable; yet, again, I considered whether my marriage would hasten my fate.
ex.zh: 那怪物若实行他的威胁，死是免不了的；可我又想，我的婚事会不会叫我的命运来得更快。

senses.d: in such a manner as could not be otherwise
x: it is necessarily so
we must needs by objective

senses.d: by necessity
x: the situation slid inescapably toward disaster

ex.t: “Remember these words to-morrow: change the course, or delay in it--for any reason--and no life can possibly be saved, and many lives must inevitably be sacrificed.”
ex.zh: “明天记住这些话：改变这条路，或者在它上面耽搁——无论什么理由——就一条命也救不了，许多条命就必然要牺牲。”

ex.t: She and Diana talked so constantly about it all day that with a stricter teacher than Mr. Phillips dire disgrace must inevitably have been their portion.
ex.zh: 她和黛安娜一整天都在谈这件事，要是老师比菲利普斯先生严些，她们准逃不了一场大祸。

ex.t: That to attempt it, would be inevitably to be torn into a quick eternity.
ex.zh: 说若去尝试，必被撕成个猝然的永生。

senses.d: that cannot be entirely consumed or used up
x: an inexhaustible supply of coal

senses.d: incapable of being entirely consumed or used up
x: an inexhaustible supply of coal

ex.t: Much as they were attached to each other, they seemed to draw inexhaustible stores of affection from a very mine of love to bestow them upon me.
The difference of manners which he observed was to him an inexhaustible source of instruction and amusement.
ex.zh: 他注意到的那些习俗的差异，于他是取之不尽的教益和乐趣的源泉。

ex.t: One had the feeling that she would have been perfectly content, if the June evening had been endless and the supply of clothes inexhaustible, to remain there for a thousand years, pegging out diapers and singing rubbish.
ex.zh: 人会觉得，要是这个六月的傍晚没有尽头，衣服也总也晾不完，她就在那儿待上一千年，夹尿布，唱胡话，也会心满意足。

senses.d: with indefatigable energy
x: she watched the show indefatigably

ex.t: The inexhaustibly interesting thing was not the fragment of coral but the interior of the glass itself.
ex.zh: 妙不可言的不是那块珊瑚，而是玻璃里面本身。

senses.d: not to be placated or appeased or moved by entreaty
x: grim determination
grim necessity

senses.d: impervious to pleas, persuasion, requests, reason- W.Churchill
x: he is adamant in his refusal to change his mind
Cynthia was inexorable; she would have none of him

ex.t: My friend is dead, my neighbour is dead, my love, the darling of my soul, is dead; it is the inexorable consolidation and perpetuation of the secret that was always in that individuality, and which I shall carry in mine to my life's end.

But the old man decidedly refused, thinking himself bound in honour to my friend, who, when he found the father inexorable, quitted his country, nor returned until he heard that his former mistress was married according to her inclinations.
Buck was inexorable.

senses.d: in an inexorable manner
x: time marches on inexorably

ex.t: It struck Goldstein's nose and bounced off; the voice continued inexorably.
ex.zh: 词典打在戈德斯坦的鼻子上，弹了开去；那声音仍旧一刻不停地继续着。

senses.d: lack of experience and the knowledge and understanding derived from experience
x: procedural inexperience created difficulties
their poor behavior was due to the rawness of the troops

ex.t: But young men didn't-at least in my provincial inexperience I believed they didn't-drift coolly out of nowhere and buy a palace on Long Island Sound.
ex.zh: 可年轻人不会——至少以我乡巴佬的阅历，我相信他们不会——冷冷地从虚无里漂出来，就在长岛海峡买下一座宫殿。

ex.t: Then, owing either to Peter's inexperience or Phyllis's good intentions, which had been rather pressing, or to some other cause, the Engine suddenly went off with a bang.
ex.zh: 后来，也许是因为彼得没经验，也许是因为菲利斯的好心肠太热心了些，也许是别的原因，那火车头忽然“砰”的一声炸了。

senses.d: lacking practical experience or training

ex.t: On the trail of the pirates, stealing noiselessly down the war-path, which is not visible to inexperienced eyes, come the redskins, every one of them with his eyes peeled.
It was one which could not fail to impress itself deeply on my mind, unfolding as it did a number of circumstances, each interesting and wonderful to one so utterly inexperienced as I was.
ex.zh: 那是一段不能不深印在我心上的来历，因为它展开的种种情形，于像我这样全然没有经验的人，每一件都有趣而奇妙。

ex.t: There they await the onslaught, the inexperienced ones clutching their revolvers and treading on twigs, but the old hands sleeping tranquilly until just before the dawn.
ex.zh: 他们在那里等着冲杀，没经验的抓着左轮枪，踩着枯枝；老手们却安睡到天亮前。

senses.d: incapable of being explained or accounted for
x: inexplicable errors
left the house at three in the morning for inexplicable reasons

ex.t: In fact, I was so afraid of him that I was not game enough just then to address him, and demand a satisfactory answer concerning what seemed inexplicable in him.
It was with great astonishment, and with a strange, inexplicable dread, that as he looked, he saw this bell begin to swing.
ex.zh: 他望着的时候，看见这只铃开始摆动，先是万分惊讶，接着又生出一种说不清道不明的古怪恐惧。

ex.t: But it seemed that, when on the wharf, Queequeg had not at all noticed what I now alluded to; hence I would have thought myself to have been optically deceived in that matter, were it not for Elijah’s otherwise inexplicable question.
ex.zh: 可看来在码头上时，魁魁格压根儿没注意我现在提到的这件事；因此，要不是以利亚那否则无法解释的问题，我倒要以为自己在这一点上是看花了眼。

senses.d: defying expression

ex.t: Gilbert had whisked the pin out of sight and was studying his history with the soberest face in the world; but when the commotion subsided he looked at Anne and winked with inexpressible drollery.
ex.zh: 吉尔伯特早把别针一晃藏了，正一脸正经得不能再正经地读历史；可等骚动平下来，他看了安妮一眼，眨眨眼，那滑稽劲儿没法形容。

ex.t: If this journey had taken place during my days of study and happiness, it would have afforded me inexpressible pleasure.
ex.zh: 若这趟旅行是在我读书和快乐的日子里，它会给我说不出的快乐。

ex.t: Through its inexpressible, strange eyes, methought I peeped to secrets which took hold of God.
ex.zh: 透过它那不可言说的、古怪的眼睛，我仿佛窥见了攥住上帝的种种秘密。

senses.d: to an inexpressible degree
x: she was looking very young tonight, and, as usual, indescribably beautiful, in a simple strapless dress of a green and white silky cotton

ex.t: Not so much in obedience, as in surprise and fear: for on the raising of the hand, he became sensible of confused noises in the air; incoherent sounds of lamentation and regret; wailings inexpressibly sorrowful and self-accusatory.
ex.zh: 与其说是听命，不如说是惊讶和害怕：因为那手一举起来，他就觉出空气里有些纷乱的声响；那是些断断续续的哀叹和悔恨；是些说不出地悲苦、又自责不已的号哭。

ex.t: At every fresh question that was put to him, this nephew burst into a fresh roar of laughter; and was so inexpressibly tickled, that he was obliged to get up off the sofa and stamp.
ex.zh: 每问一个新问题，这外甥就爆发出一阵新的大笑；他被逗得说不出地开心，不得不从沙发上站起来跺脚。

ex.t: It is so inexpressibly comfortable to have you here,” was Meg’s answer.
ex.zh: 有您在这儿，真是说不出的舒坦，”梅格回答。

senses.d: not expressive
x: an inexpressive face

ex.t: Where any name happens to be vague or inexpressive, I shall say so, and suggest another.
ex.zh: 倘若哪个名字碰巧含混或不达意，我就说明，并另提一个。

senses.d: difficult or impossible to extinguish
x: an inextinguishable flame
an inextinguishable faith

ex.t: Even although we meet as strangers now I still love her with an inextinguishable love.
ex.zh: 虽然我们现在见了面像陌生人，我仍旧爱她，这爱是扑不灭的。

ex.t: I will revenge my injuries; if I cannot inspire love, I will cause fear, and chiefly towards you my arch-enemy, because my creator, do I swear inextinguishable hatred.
ex.zh: 我要为我的伤害报仇；我若不能使人爱我，就要使人怕我，尤其是对你，我的大仇人，因为你是我的造物者，我立誓永不熄灭的仇恨。

ex.t: At first my efforts met with a stare of surprise or inextinguishable laughter, but presently a fair-haired little creature seemed to grasp my intention and repeated a name.
ex.zh: 起初我的努力换来的是惊讶的瞪视或止不住的大笑，但不久一个金发的小人似乎明白了我的意思，重复了一个名称。

senses.d: in an inextricable manner
x: motives inspired by Mammon were often inextricably blended with things pertaining to Caesar and to God

ex.t: In his mind the smell of it was inextricably mixed up with fornication.
ex.zh: 在他心里，那气味和私通不可分割地混在一起。

senses.d: the quality of never making an error

ex.t: But by far the more important reason for the readjustment of the past is the need to safeguard the infallibility of the Party.
ex.zh: 但重新调整过去，重要得多的理由是必须维护党的绝无错误。

ex.t: For the secret of rulership is to combine a belief in one's own infallibility with the Power to learn from past mistakes.
ex.zh: 因为统治的秘诀，是把对自己绝无错误的信念，同从过去错误中学习的能力结合起来。

senses.d: incapable of failure or error
x: an infallible antidote
an infallible memory

ex.t: Again the mender of roads went through the whole performance; in which he ought to have been perfect by that time, seeing that it had been the infallible resource and indispensable entertainment of his village during a whole year.
ex.zh: 修路人又把整套动作演了一遍；到这时候他本该演得炉火纯青了，因为整整一年里，这始终是他村子里万无一失的招数、不可或缺的消遣。

ex.t: I will not lead you on, unguarded and ardent as I then was, to your destruction and infallible misery.
ex.zh: 我不愿像当年我自己那样毫无防备又满腔热望，把你引向毁灭和那无可避免的苦难。

ex.t: I was a good Christian; born and bred in the bosom of the infallible Presbyterian Church.
ex.zh: 我是个虔诚的基督徒；生在绝无谬误的长老会的怀抱里，长在那怀抱里。

senses.d: known widely and usually unfavorably
x: a notorious gangster
the tenderloin district was notorious for vice

ex.t: Far in this den of infamous resort, there was a low-browed, beetling shop, below a pent-house roof, where iron, old rags, bottles, bones, and greasy offal, were bought.
ex.zh: 在这声名狼藉的去处深处，有一家屋檐低垂、向前突出的铺子，上头搭着个单坡的棚顶，收购铁器、破布、瓶子、骨头和油腻的下水。

ex.t: They hanged at Tyburn, in those days, so the street outside Newgate had not obtained one infamous notoriety that has since attached to it.
ex.zh: 那时候他们是在泰伯恩行刑，所以新门监狱外那条街还没有后来附在它身上的那种臭名。

ex.t: It was an infamous prosecution, grossly infamous; but not the less likely to succeed on that account.”
ex.zh: 那是一场卑鄙的起诉，卑鄙透顶；可也并不因此就少一分成功的可能。”

senses.d: a state of extreme dishonor- F.D.Roosevelt
x: a date which will live in infamy
the name was a by-word of scorn and opprobrium throughout the city

senses.d: evil fame or public reputation

ex.t: Some passing thought of the infamy and disgrace for which it had been reserved, may have struck the prisoner’s mind.
ex.zh: 犯人心里也许闪过了这样一个念头：这面镜子留着，是为了何等样的耻辱和丢脸。

ex.t: That, he had been the prisoner’s friend, but, at once in an auspicious and an evil hour detecting his infamy, had resolved to immolate the traitor he could no longer cherish in his bosom, on the sacred altar of his country.
ex.zh: 他本来是犯人的朋友，可是在一个既吉利又凶险的时刻察觉了他的邪恶，便决心把这个他再也不能放在怀里珍爱的叛徒，献祭在祖国的圣坛上。

ex.t: Be that as it may, she saw him go with regret; and in this early example of what Lydia’s infamy must produce, found additional anguish as she reflected on that wretched business.
ex.zh: 不管怎样，她看着他走，心里难过；而这是莉迪亚的丑事必定要生出的头一个例子，她一想到那桩不幸的事，便又添了几分痛苦。

senses.d: the early stage of growth or development
the earliest state of immaturity

ex.t: To say that he was not startled, or that his blood was not conscious of a terrible sensation to which it had been a stranger from infancy, would be untrue.
ex.zh: 要说他没受惊，要说他的血没有感到一种从婴孩时起就未曾有过的骇人感觉，那是不真切的。

ex.t: I know, Doctor Manette--how can I fail to know--that, mingled with the affection and duty of a daughter who has become a woman, there is, in her heart, towards you, all the love and reliance of infancy itself.
ex.zh: 我知道，马内特医生——我怎么会不知道——在她那颗已经长成女人的女儿的心里，对她的爱与孝里，还掺着婴孩时期全部的爱和依赖。

ex.t: Towards Soho, therefore, Mr. Stryver shouldered his way from the Temple, while the bloom of the Long Vacation’s infancy was still upon it.
ex.zh: 于是，趁着长假的幼年还带着它的鲜花，斯特赖弗先生从圣殿区一路挤向索霍。

senses.d: a very young child (birth to 1 year) who has not yet begun to walk or talk
x: the baby began to cry again
she held the baby in her arms

ex.t: I, their eldest child, was born at Naples, and as an infant accompanied them in their rambles.
The infant had been placed with these good people to nurse: they were better off then.

He had been quite familiar with one old ghost, in a white waistcoat, with a monstrous iron safe attached to its ankle, who cried piteously at being unable to assist a wretched woman with an infant, whom it saw below, upon a door-step.
ex.zh: 有一个穿白马甲的鬼，他熟得很；那鬼脚踝上拴着一只奇大无比的铁保险箱，它看见下面门槛上坐着一个抱着婴儿的苦命女人，却没法去帮她，就哀哀地哭。

senses.d: indicating a lack of maturity
x: childish tantrums
infantile behavior

senses.d: of or relating to infants or infancy
x: infantile paralysis

senses.d: being or befitting or characteristic of an infant
x: infantile games

ex.t: Hold me up, Jo, for upon my life it’s one too many for me,” returned Laurie, regarding the infants with the air of a big, benevolent Newfoundland looking at a pair of infantile kittens.
ex.zh: 乔，扶着我，我这辈子真招架不住了，”劳里答道，看那两个婴孩的神气，像一条和善的大纽芬兰狗看着一对小猫崽。

senses.d: an army unit consisting of soldiers who fight on foot
x: there came ten thousand horsemen and as many fully-armed foot

ex.t: The Gupta chess pieces were divided, like their military, into the infantry, cavalry, elephants, and chariots.
I was in the Twenty-eighth Infantry."
ex.zh: 我在第二十八步兵团。”

ex.t: In the Argonne Forest I took the remains of my machine-gun battalion so far forward that there was a half mile gap on either side of us where the infantry couldn't advance.
ex.zh: 在阿戈讷森林，我带着机枪营剩下的弟兄推进得太远，两翼各留出半英里的空当，步兵根本跟不上来。

senses.d: a very young child (birth to 1 year) who has not yet begun to walk or talk
x: the baby began to cry again
she held the baby in her arms

ex.t: Hold me up, Jo, for upon my life it’s one too many for me,” returned Laurie, regarding the infants with the air of a big, benevolent Newfoundland looking at a pair of infantile kittens.
ex.zh: 乔，扶着我，我这辈子真招架不住了，”劳里答道，看那两个婴孩的神气，像一条和善的大纽芬兰狗看着一对小猫崽。

ex.t: Zogranda, one of their most famous doctors, recommends strips of blubber for infants, as being exceedingly juicy and nourishing.
ex.zh: 他们最有名的一位医生佐格兰达，主张给婴儿吃鲸脂条，说它极多汁、极滋养。

ex.t: One of these little infants, that from certain queer tokens seemed hardly a day old, might have measured some fourteen feet in length, and some six feet in girth.
ex.zh: 这些小家伙里有一头，从某些古怪的迹象看，似乎还不到一天大，身长也许有十四英尺，腰围六英尺。

senses.d: marked by foolish or unreasoning fondness
x: he was infatuated with her
Narcissus was a beautiful Greek youth who became enamored of his own reflection

ex.t: I never saw such an infatuated man.
ex.zh: 我没见过这么着迷的人。

ex.t: Josie said you were infatuated with her.”
ex.zh: 乔西说你迷上她了。”

ex.t: Seeing, however, that his forbearance had not the slightest effect, by an awful and unspeakable intimation with his twisted hand he warned off the foolish and infatuated man; but it was to no purpose.
ex.zh: 可他看出自己的克制没有半点效果，便用扭弯的手做出一个可怕而说不出的示意，警告那愚蠢而迷了心的人退开；可全无用处。

senses.d: a foolish and usually extravagant passion or love or admiration
temporary love of an adolescent
an object of extravagant short-lived passion

ex.zh: “当然；若拿我自己的好奇心去烦扰你，那才真是无礼又无情。”

ex.zh: 他是折磨者，他是保护者，他是审问者，他是朋友。

ex.zh: 这趟旅行是我自己提议的，伊丽莎白因此也就依了，可一想到我要离开她，受困苦和忧愁的侵袭，她便满心不安。

ex.zh: 至于科迪莉亚，她悔恨得发了疯，被关进了疯人院。

ex.t: I began to grow vexed with him; it seemed so downright senseless and insane to be sitting there all day and half the night on his hams in a cold room, holding a piece of wood on his head.
ex.zh: 我开始对他恼火了；在一个冷屋子里蹲一整天外加半夜，头上顶着一块木头，这显得太荒唐、太没有道理。

ex.zh: 记忆把疯狂一同带来；我一想到过去的事，就真的发起疯来；有时我狂怒，烧着怒火；有时我低沉绝望。

ex.t: There’s the fruits of promotion now; there’s the vanity of glory: there’s the insanity of life!
ex.zh: 这就是升迁的果实；这就是荣名的虚幻：这就是人生的疯狂！

ex.zh: 我一想到下一个被他那不知足的报复牺牲的会是谁，就发抖。

ex.zh: 它缓缓地、越来越远地漂开去；周围的海水被贪得无厌的鲨鱼搅得翻腾四溅，上方的空气被一群群尖叫着、贪馋的飞鸟搅得不安，它们的喙插在鲸身上，像许多把侮辱人的短剑。

Hunger was the inscription on the baker’s shelves, written in every small loaf of his scanty stock of bad bread; at the sausage-shop, in every dead-dog preparation that was offered for sale.

ex.zh: 人们在刻字下方的地面仔细查验，在一块石头、一片砖或者某块铺地碎片的底下的土里，发现了一张纸的灰烬，跟一只小皮盒或小皮袋的灰烬混在一起。

ex.zh: 你不知道自己的脸是什么样子，就不容易保持莫测。

ex.zh: 给任何比他弱小的生灵制造痛苦，似乎就是他唯一的消遣念头；他在谋划捕捉老鼠、小鸟和昆虫上还显出非凡的才能。

ex.zh: 人类的一切声音，羊的咩叫，鸟的鸣啭，虫的嗡鸣，构成我们生活背景的那种骚动——全都结束了。

ex.zh: 他忽然想到，现代生活真正特有的东西不是它的残酷和不安全，而只是它的空乏，它的晦暗，它的无精打采。

ex.zh: 不错，他把胡克的胳膊扔给了鳄鱼，可即便这一件事，加上因此而来的、由鳄鱼那份不死心造成的生活里更大的不安稳，也难解释这样毫不放松、这样恶毒的报复心。

ex.zh: “也许正是这种不安、这种不踏实，驱使我一次次跑得更远去探查。

ex.zh: 可一个人一旦疑心有什么不对，有时候会这样：他既然已经卷进这件事里，就会不知不觉地竭力把疑心掩盖起来，连对自己也掩盖。

ex.zh: 对我是够安全的；那儿有那么多更值得去干涉的人，谁也不会费心去干涉一个快八十的老头子。

ex.zh: 通向宅子的是碎石车道，弯弯曲曲穿过宽阔的草坪，又从高大白杨交错的枝桠下经过。

senses.d: linked or locked closely together as by dovetailing

ex.zh: 听我说，小子——四肢飞快地交缠——柔韧的摇摆——娇羞——颤动！嘴唇！心！胯！全都擦着边：不停地一碰就离！不是品尝，你们要明白，否则饱足就来了。

ex.t: As, after this interlude, the seamen resumed their work upon the jacket of the whale, many strange things were hinted in reference to this wild affair.
ex.zh: 这场插曲过后，水手们重新动手处理鲸的外皮，关于这桩荒唐事，人们暗示了许多离奇的猜测。

ex.zh: 可是——说真的，您知道，斯特赖弗先生——”洛里先生停住，用最古怪的样子对他摇头，仿佛他不由自主地在心里补了一句：“你知道，你实在是太多、太多了！”
