irony is wasted on the stupid

senses.d: incongruity between what might be expected and what actually occurs
x: the irony of Ireland's copying the nation she most hated

senses.d: a trope that involves incongruity between what is expected and what occurs

ex.t: More even than of strength, he gave an impression of confidence and of an understanding tinged by irony.
ex.zh: 他给人的印象甚至不只是力量，而是一种自信，一种带点嘲讽的通达。

ex.t: 'What shall it be this time?' he said, still with the same faint suggestion of irony.
ex.zh: “这次为什么喝？”他说，仍旧带着那点淡淡的讥讽。

ex.t: 'They got me a long time ago,' said O'Brien with a mild, almost regretful irony.
ex.zh: “他们很久以前就抓住我了，”奥布莱恩带着温和的、几乎带歉意的嘲讽说。

senses.d: give spiritual insight to; in religion
cast rays of light upon
expose to radiation
x: irradiate food

ex.t: For, d’ye see, rainbows do not visit the clear air; they only irradiate vapor.
ex.zh: 因为，你瞧，虹不到清朗的空气里去；它只照临雾气。

senses.d: give spiritual insight to; in religion
cast rays of light upon
expose to radiation
x: irradiate food

ex.t: The warning seemed not unnecessary, so uplifted and aerial was Anne’s expression and attitude as she sprang to her feet, her face irradiated with the flame of her spirit.
ex.zh: 这警告似乎并不多余，因为安妮跳起来的时候，那神情、那姿态，真是又高又飘，脸上像燃着她灵魂的火光。

senses.d: the condition of being exposed to radiation
a column of light (as from a beacon)
(physiology) the spread of sensory neural impulses in the cortex
the apparent enlargement of a bright object when viewed against a dark background
(Pavolvian conditioning) the elicitation of a conditioned response by stimulation similar but not identical to the original stimulus
(medicine) the treatment of disease (especially cancer) by exposure to a radioactive substance

ex.t: About half an hour afterwards he attempted again to speak but was unable; he pressed my hand feebly, and his eyes closed for ever, while the irradiation of a gentle smile passed away from his lips.
ex.zh: 大约半个钟头后，他又想说话，可说不出来；他无力地握了握我的手，眼睛永远闭上了，同时一丝温和的笑从他唇上消去。

senses.d: not consistent with or using reason
x: irrational fears
irrational animals

senses.d: real but not expressible as the quotient of two integers
x: irrational numbers

senses.d: a real number that cannot be expressed as a rational number

ex.t: Jupiter, seeing that Mankind, the only rational creatures, were far outnumbered by the irrational beasts, bade him redress the balance by turning some of the latter into men.
ex.zh: 朱庇特见人类是唯一有理性的造物，数目却远不及无理性的兽类，就叫他补救这个失衡，把一些兽变成人。

senses.d: impossible to reconcile
x: irreconcilable differences

ex.t: The aims of these groups are entirely irreconcilable...
ex.zh: 这些群体的目标完全无法调和……

ex.t:
He continued reading:

The aims of these three groups are entirely irreconcilable.
ex.zh:
他接着读：

这三个集团的目标完全无法调和。

senses.d: contrary to rule or accepted order or general practice
x: irregular hiring practices

senses.d: not occurring at a regular rate or fixed intervals
x: an irregular heartbeat

senses.d: (used of the military) not belonging to or engaged in by regular army forces
x: irregular troops
irregular warfare

senses.d: (of solids) not having clear dimensions that can be measured; volume must be determined with the principle of liquid displacement
failing to meet a standard of manufacture due to an imperfection
x: an irregular pair of jeans

senses.d: deviating from normal expectations; somewhat odd, strange, or abnormal
x: these days large families are atypical
atypical clinical findings

ex.t: About two o'clock the mist cleared away, and we beheld, stretched out in every direction, vast and irregular plains of ice, which seemed to have no end.
By this definition, Pluto was not a planet due to its irregular orbit and size.
About two o’clock the mist cleared away, and we beheld, stretched out in every direction, vast and irregular plains of ice, which seemed to have no end.
ex.zh: 约莫两点钟，雾散了，我们望见四面八方铺展着一片片广袤而不齐整的冰原，仿佛没有尽头。

senses.d: behavior that breaches the rule or etiquette or custom or morality
not characterized by a fixed principle or rate; at irregular intervals
an irregular asymmetry in shape; an irregular spatial pattern
irregular and infrequent or difficult evacuation of the bowels; can be a symptom of intestinal obstruction or diverticulitis

ex.t: There were also certain irregularities in word-formation arising out of the need for rapid and easy speech.
ex.zh: 构词上也有一些不规则之处，源于说话求快求易的需要。

senses.d: behavior that breaches the rule or etiquette or custom or morality
not characterized by a fixed principle or rate; at irregular intervals
an irregular asymmetry in shape; an irregular spatial pattern
irregular and infrequent or difficult evacuation of the bowels; can be a symptom of intestinal obstruction or diverticulitis

ex.t: You can hold your tongue and, moreover, you can time any little irregularity of your own so that everybody else is so blind that they don't see or care.

senses.d: at an uneven rate
x: the patient is breathing irregularly

senses.d: having an irregular form
x: irregularly shaped solids

senses.d: in an irregular manner
x: her letters arrived irregularly

ex.t: The whales had irregularly settled bodily down into the blue, thus giving no distantly discernible token of the movement, though from his closer vicinity Ahab had observed it.
ex.zh: 那些鲸已经零乱地整个儿沉进碧蓝的海里，因此从远处看不出这动作的任何迹象，虽然亚哈因离得近，已经觉察到了。

ex.t: The only classes of words that were still allowed to inflect irregularly were the pronouns, the relatives, the demonstrative adjectives, and the auxiliary verbs.
ex.zh: 仍被允许不规则变化的词类只有代词、关系词、指示形容词和助动词。

ex.t: With little ripples that were hardly the shadows of waves, the laden mattress moved irregularly down the pool.
ex.zh: 载着人的气垫顺着池子不规则地漂动，泛起的细纹几乎算不上波浪的影子。

senses.d: having no bearing on or connection with the subject at issue
x: an irrelevant comment
irrelevant allegations

ex.t: (I've heard it said that Daisy's murmur was only to make people lean toward her; an irrelevant criticism that made it no less charming.)
ex.zh: （我听人说过，黛西的低语只是为了让人朝她凑近些；这批评虽不相干，却并没让她减色半分。）

senses.d: in an irrelevant manner
x: suddenly and irrelevantly, she asked him for money

ex.t: Then she added irrelevantly: "You ought to see the baby."
ex.zh: 接着她又没头没脑地补了一句：“你该看看那孩子。”

senses.d: hostile or indifferent to religion

ex.t: If you’re a religious woman, give me a irreligious one!
ex.zh: 你要是个信教的女人，那还不如给我个不信教的！

senses.d: impossible to remedy or correct or redress
x: an irremediable error
irremediable defects of character

ex.t: I have devoted my creator, the select specimen of all that is worthy of love and admiration among men, to misery; I have pursued him even to that irremediable ruin.
ex.zh: 我把我的造物主——人中一切可爱可敬之物的精选标本——送进了苦里；我一直追他，追到那无可挽救的毁败。

ex.t: Elizabeth particularly, who knew that her mother owed to the latter the preservation of her favourite daughter from irremediable infamy, was hurt and distressed to a most painful degree by a distinction so ill applied.
ex.zh: 伊丽莎白尤其难受：她知道母亲最心疼的女儿，全亏后者才免于身败名裂；这样一份客气用错了地方，叫她痛心到极点。

senses.d: impossible to repair, rectify, or amend
x: irreparable harm
an irreparable mistake

ex.t: I need not describe the feelings of those whose dearest ties are rent by that most irreparable evil, the void that presents itself to the soul, and the despair that is exhibited on the countenance.
“I can offer you no consolation, my friend,” said he; “your disaster is irreparable.
ex.zh: “我没法给你安慰，我的朋友，”他说，“你的灾难无可补救。

ex.t: He could have endured poverty, and while this distress had been the meed of his virtue, he gloried in it; but the ingratitude of the Turk and the loss of his beloved Safie were misfortunes more bitter and irreparable.
ex.zh: 他本来受得住贫穷；当这困苦是他美德的报酬时，他还以此自豪；可那土耳其人的忘恩负义和失去他心爱的莎菲，是更苦更不可弥补的不幸。

senses.d: impossible to repress or control
x: an irrepressible chatterbox
uncontrollable laughter

ex.t: The scaling him with chairs for ladders to dive into his pockets, despoil him of brown-paper parcels, hold on tight by his cravat, hug him round his neck, pommel his back, and kick his legs in irrepressible affection!
The old man uttered an irrepressible cry.
ex.zh: 老人发出一声抑制不住的叫喊。

ex.t: But, her courage was of that emotional nature that it brought the irrepressible tears into her eyes.
ex.zh: 可她的勇气是那种动感情的性质，竟叫止不住的泪涌进她眼里。

senses.d: free of guilt; not subject to blame
x: has lived a blameless life
of irreproachable character

ex.t: Anne started off irreproachable, arrayed in the stiff black-and-white sateen, which, while decent as regards length and certainly not open to the charge of skimpiness, contrived to emphasize every corner and angle of her thin figure.
ex.zh: 安妮出门时无可挑剔，穿着那件硬邦邦的黑白棉缎；那衣裳长度上还算体面，也绝挑不出窄小的毛病，却偏把她瘦削身架上的每一个棱角都衬了出来。

ex.t: Elizabeth saw even this last resource, her excellent dispositions and irreproachable conduct, about to fail the accused, when, although violently agitated, she desired permission to address the court.
ex.zh: 伊丽莎白眼看连这最后一条路——她优良的品性和无可指责的操守——也要在这被告身上失效，便虽然激动得厉害，仍请求准许向法庭说话。

ex.t: “The conduct of neither, if strictly examined, will be irreproachable; but since then we have both, I hope, improved in civility.”
ex.zh: “严格说来，两人的举止都算不上无可指摘；不过从那以后，我希望我们都变得有礼些了。”

senses.d: impossible to resist; overpowering
x: irresistible (or resistless) impulses
what happens when an irresistible force meets an immovable object?

senses.d: overpoweringly attractive
x: irresistible beauty

ex.t: Irresistible impulses seized him.
When I have learned a Truth like this, I know how strong and irresistible it must be.
ex.zh: 我既明白了这样一个道理，就知道它有多强、多不可抗拒。

ex.t: He was conscious of being exhausted, and overcome by an irresistible drowsiness; and, further, of being in his own bedroom.
ex.zh: 他觉得自己筋疲力尽，被一股无法抗拒的睡意压倒；还发觉自己已经在自己卧室里。

senses.d: the quality of being overpowering and impossible to resist

ex.t: If this be so, fancy the irresistibleness of that might, to which the most impalpable and destructive of all elements contributes.
ex.zh: 倘若果真如此，那就想想那股力量何等不可抗拒吧——一切元素中最不可捉摸、也最具破坏性的那一种，也来助它一臂之力。

senses.d: incapable of being resisted
x: the candy looked overwhelmingly desirable to the dieting man

ex.t: It is a fair, even-handed, noble adjustment of things, that while there is infection in disease and sorrow, there is nothing in the world so irresistibly contagious as laughter and good-humour.
ex.zh: 这世上的安排真是公平、公道、高尚：疾病和忧愁会传染，可天下再没有比笑声和好脾气更容易传染的了。

ex.t: He looked so irresistibly pleasant, in a word, that three or four good-humoured fellows said, "Good morning, sir!
ex.zh: 一句话，他看上去快活得叫人招架不住，三四个脾气好的人便说：“早上好，先生！

ex.t: I feel irresistibly tempted to do it.
ex.zh: 我觉得有一种挡不住的引诱。

senses.d: uncertain how to act or proceed
x: the committee was timid and mediocre and irresolute

ex.t: From being irresolute and purposeless, his feet became animated by an intention, and, in the working out of that intention, they took him to the Doctor’s door.
ex.zh: 他的脚步本来犹疑无目的，这时被一个意图催动起来；在实行那意图的过程中，脚步把他带到了医生家门口。

ex.t: But I stood irresolute; when looking at a clock in the corner, he exclaimed “I vum it’s Sunday—you won’t see that harpooneer to-night; he’s come to anchor somewhere—come along then; do come; won’t ye come?”
ex.zh: 可我还站着迟疑；他看了看角落里的一只钟，叫道：“我敢说已经是礼拜天了——你今晚见不着那个鱼叉手了；他不知在哪儿下了锚——那就来吧；来呀；你到底来不来？”

senses.d: lacking determination or decisiveness

ex.t: “Do you mean that you won’t say, sir?” the spy irresolutely asked.
ex.zh: “你的意思是你不肯说吗，先生？”探子犹疑地问。

ex.t: He followed irresolutely for a little distance, half a pace behind her.
ex.zh: 他犹犹豫豫地跟了一小段，落在她半步之后。

ex.t: A moisture came into his eyes, and, as the whipping continued, he arose and walked irresolutely up and down.
ex.zh: 他眼里泛起湿意；鞭打还在继续，他站起来，犹疑地来回走。

senses.d: doubt concerning two or more possible alternatives or courses of action
x: his indecision was only momentary but the opportunity was lost

senses.d: the trait of being irresolute; lacking firmness of purpose

ex.t: He did pause, with a moment's irresolution, before he shut the door; and he did look cautiously behind it first, as if he half expected to be terrified with the sight of Marley's pigtail sticking out into the hall.
“The hour of my irresolution is past, and the period of your power is arrived.
ex.zh: “我犹豫的时期过去了，你掌权的时期到了。

senses.d: in spite of everything; without regard to drawbacks
x: he carried on regardless of the difficulties

ex.t: Only a very few words were common to all lists, and there was no vocabulary expressing the function of Science as a habit of mind, or a method of thought, irrespective of its particular branches.
ex.zh: 所有词表共有的词极少，而且没有一套词汇用来表达科学作为一种思维习惯或思想方法的功能，而不论其具体分支。

senses.d: showing lack of care for consequences
x: behaved like an irresponsible idiot
hasty and irresponsible action

ex.t: While wars could be won or lost, no ruling class could be completely irresponsible.
He was brilliant, fantastic, irresponsible.
ex.zh: 他光彩四射，怪诞，不负责任。

senses.d: impossible to recover or recoup or overcome
x: an irretrievable loss
irretrievable errors in judgment

ex.t: But I did not believe my errors to be irretrievable, and after much consideration I resolved to return to the cottage, seek the old man, and by my representations win him to my party.
ex.zh: 可我不相信我的错是不可挽回的，想了许久之后，我决心回到农舍去找那老人，用我的陈述把他拉到我这方面来。

ex.t: But was it all irretrievable?
ex.zh: 可这一切都无可挽回了吗？

senses.d: in an irretrievable manner
x: it is irretrievably lost

ex.t: I, who irretrievably destroyed thee by destroying all thou lovedst.
ex.zh: 是我，毁了你所爱的一切，把你无可挽回地毁了。

senses.d: an irreverent mental attitude
a disrespectful act

ex.t: Poor Marilla was only preserved from complete collapse by remembering that it was not irreverence, but simply spiritual ignorance on the part of Anne that was responsible for this extraordinary petition.
ex.zh: 可怜的玛丽拉差点儿整个儿垮掉，全靠想起来：这篇离奇的祷词该怪的不是不敬，而只是安妮在灵性上的无知。

ex.t: As if long habituated to such profane talk from his old shipmate, Bildad, without noticing his present irreverence, quietly looked up, and seeing me, glanced again inquiringly towards Peleg.
ex.zh: 比勒达仿佛早就听惯了老船友这种不敬的话，也不理会他此刻的失礼，只静静地抬起眼来，看见了我，就又带着询问的神气朝佩莱格看了一眼。

ex.t: But there was no sign of reawakening courage in his followers, rather, indeed, of growing terror at the irreverence of his words.
ex.zh: 可他手下没有一点重新鼓起勇气的迹象，倒是对他这番不敬的话越来越怕。

senses.d: showing lack of due respect or veneration
x: irreverent scholars mocking sacred things
noisy irreverent tourists

senses.d: characterized by a lightly pert and exuberant quality
x: a certain irreverent gaiety and ease of manner

senses.d: not revering god

ex.t: It’s irreverent--positively irreverent.”
ex.zh: 这是不敬——简直是不敬。”

ex.t: I’m sure I didn’t mean to be irreverent.”
ex.zh: 我敢说我一点没有不敬的意思。”

ex.t: After a moment she added as if she might have sounded irreverent, "There wasn't any connection."
ex.zh: 过了一会儿，她像是怕自己听上去不敬，又添了一句：“这里头没什么关联。”

senses.d: incapable of being retracted or revoked- Shakespeare
x: firm and irrevocable is my doom

ex.t: Even after enormous upheavals and seemingly irrevocable changes, the same pattern has always reasserted itself, just as a gyroscope will always return to equilibrium, however far it is pushed one way or the other.
ex.zh: 即使经过巨大的动乱和看来不可逆转的变化，同一个模式也总会重新确立，就像陀螺无论被推向哪一边多远，总要回到平衡。

ex.t: An irrevocable vow.
ex.zh: 一个不可撤销的誓约。

ex.t: It is an irrevocable vow that I want to take.
ex.zh: 我要立的正是这个不可撤销的誓约。

senses.d: in an irrevocable manner

ex.t: Everywhere I see bliss, from which I alone am irrevocably excluded.
ex.zh: 我到处看见福乐，唯独我被永远排除在外。

ex.t: However, it is always as well to have a look at him before irrevocably committing yourself into his hands.
ex.zh: 不过，在把自己不可挽回地交到他手里之前，先看他一眼总是好的。

ex.t: I knew enough of your disposition to be certain, that had you been absolutely, irrevocably decided against me, you would have acknowledged it to Lady Catherine frankly and openly.”
ex.zh: 你的性情我知道得够多，可以断定：你要是真已铁了心、无可挽回地拒绝我，你一定会对凯瑟琳夫人坦白直说。”

senses.d: supplying dry land with water by means of ditches etc
(medicine) cleaning a wound or body organ by flushing or washing out with water or a medicated solution

ex.t: And the seeds of vegetables rarely come to much in a soil that is constantly disturbed for the purposes of war and irrigation.
ex.zh: 而菜种在为了战争和灌溉不断翻动的土里，是很少长出什么的。

senses.d: an irritable petulant feeling
excessive sensitivity of an organ or body part
a disposition to exhibit uncontrolled anger
x: his temper was well known to all his employees

ex.t: Perpetual fretting at length threw Madame Moritz into a decline, which at first increased her irritability, but she is now at peace for ever.
ex.zh: 无休止的烦躁终于把莫里茨夫人拖成了痨症，起初只叫她更易发火，可她如今永远安息了。

ex.t: Their irritability arose out of their misery, increased with it, doubled upon it, outdistanced it.
ex.zh: 他们的火气从苦里来，跟着苦长，翻着倍地长，跑到苦前头去了。

senses.d: easily irritated or annoyed
x: an incorrigibly fractious young man
not the least nettlesome of his countrymen

senses.d: abnormally sensitive to a stimulus
capable of responding to stimuli

ex.t: But she is naturally a more irritable constitution than the black horse; flies tease her more; anything wrong in the harness frets her more; and if she were ill-used or unfairly treated she would not be unlikely to give tit for tat.
ex.zh: 可她天生比那匹黑马性子急；苍蝇更招她烦，挽具哪儿不对劲，她更受不住；要是有人虐待她、亏待她，她多半是要一报还一报的。

ex.t: Catherine, weak-spirited, irritable, and completely under Lydia’s guidance, had been always affronted by their advice; and Lydia, self-willed and careless, would scarcely give them a hearing.
ex.zh: 凯瑟琳性子软弱、容易动气，又全听莉迪亚的指挥，一向听不进她们的劝；莉迪亚任性又不经心，简直不肯听她们说。

ex.t: She was not of so ungovernable a temper as Lydia; and, removed from the influence of Lydia’s example, she became, by proper attention and management, less irritable, less ignorant, and less insipid.
ex.zh: 她的性子不像莉迪亚那样管不住；一离开莉迪亚的榜样，再加上好好的照看和管教，她便不那么爱生气，不那么无知，也不那么乏味了。

senses.d: in a petulant manner
x: he said testily: `Go away!'

senses.d: in an irritable manner
x: she had become irritably exact

ex.t: Even now it was quite conceivable that he was simply a busy man wondering irritably why he had been interrupted.
ex.zh: 就算到这会儿，也完全可能他只是一个忙人，正烦躁地纳闷自己为什么被打搅。

senses.d: cause annoyance in; disturb, especially by minor irritations
x: Mosquitoes buzzing in my ear really bothers me
It irritates me that she never closes the door after she leaves

senses.d: excite to an abnormal condition, or chafe or inflame
x: Aspirin irritates my stomach

senses.d: excite to some characteristic action or condition, such as motion, contraction, or nervous impulse, by the application of a stimulus
x: irritate the glands of a leaf

ex.t: This speech which would have softened good Mrs. Lynde’s heart in a twinkling, had no effect on Mrs. Barry except to irritate her still more.
ex.zh: 这番话要是说给好心的林德太太听，一颗心立时就能软下来，可对巴里太太却毫无作用，只把她惹得更恼。

ex.t: “Don’t irritate him unnecessarily,” had been Wendy’s instructions in the hold; so Tootles stepped forward politely.
ex.zh: “别无缘无故惹他。”这是温迪在货舱里的嘱咐；所以图图礼貌地走上前。

senses.d: aroused to impatience or anger
x: made an irritated gesture
feeling nettled from the constant teasing

ex.t: Alice felt a little irritated at the Caterpillar’s making such very short remarks, and she drew herself up and said, very gravely, “I think, you ought to tell me who you are, first.”
ex.zh: 毛毛虫说话这么短，爱丽丝有点恼了，她挺直身子，非常严肃地说：“我想，你应该先告诉我你是谁。”

ex.t: Consequently, when Marilla entered her kitchen and found the fire black out, with no sign of Anne anywhere, she felt justly disappointed and irritated.
ex.zh: 所以，玛丽拉进了厨房，看见炉火黑着，安妮连影子也不见，她的失望和气恼是应当的。

ex.t: That hiss, faint as it was, irritated the irascible gentleman, and sealed the culprit’s fate.
ex.zh: 那一声嘘虽然轻，却惹恼了这位暴躁的先生，也就定了这犯过错的人的命。

senses.d: causing irritation or annoyance
